Wider Sports News.title: Will the NFL get its way on early TV deal renegotiations amid courtroom and broadcaster resistance?
Wider Sports News.summary: The NFL holds by far the most lucrative broadcast deals in sport but in recent months, it has begun moves to renew those partnerships several years early to secure even revenues. Yet for all its power and popularity, its efforts could stall in the face of legislative and commercial obstacles. The post Will the NFL get its way on early TV deal renegotiations amid courtroom and broadcaster resistance? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The National Football League’s (NFL) domestic broadcast deals are the envy of almost every rights holder on the planet. Back in 2021, it guaranteed its status as sport’s richest league for another decade. A new set of broadcast contracts – running from the 2023 season until 2033 – secured US$111 billion from CBS, Fox, NBC, ESPN and Amazon.

Further deals for one-off matchups, the Sunday Ticket package of out-of-market matchups, and a global partnership for select set-piece games with Netflix, including Christmas Day, have increased this revenue stream even further.

Wider Sports News.title: Pools revealed for rugby sevens at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
Wider Sports News.summary: Pools revealed for rugby sevens at Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games HSBC SVNS Series
Wider Sports News.body:
Rugby sevens will return to the Youth Olympic Games for the third time when some of the world’s most promising young players take to the field at Dakar 2026. The Opening Ceremony is on 31 October and the rugby tournament kicks off at the 8,000-seat Complexe Iba Mar Diop the following day, with medals awarded on 2 and 3 November. Dakar 2026 is set to make history as the first Olympic sporting event to be staged on the African continent. Around 2,700 young athletes are expected to compete across 25 competition sports.

Eight men’s and eight women’s rugby sevens teams have qualified for Dakar 2026, with the competitions featuring two pools of four teams. Australia, China, Kenya and hosts Senegal will compete in Pool A, while Pool B features Czechia, Madagascar, Spain and USA.

Wider Sports News.title: Why Birmingham Phoenix chose strategy over cash in the Hundred’s franchise sell-off
Wider Sports News.summary: The 2026 season marks the first time the impact of the Hundred’s new team owners has been clearly visible across the ECB’s 100-ball cricket competition. While some franchises have traded elements of their identity for investment, Warwickshire CEO Stuart Cain explains why Birmingham’s brand and long-term interests were always non-negotiable. The post Why Birmingham Phoenix chose strategy over cash in the Hundred’s franchise sell-off appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The sixth edition of the Hundred is by far and away the most significant campaign of the 100-ball franchise cricket competition since it debuted five years ago. The 2026 season is the first since the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) permitted outside investment into its eight constituent franchises, a process which has raised UK£500 million that will be used to shore up the grassroots and county game.

Investors include some of the biggest technology companies in the world, private equity firms, and the backers of Indian Premier League (IPL) teams. The off-season has been marked by rebranding exercises, greater outlays on playing staff, and a shift from centralised governance that has put more power into the hands of individual franchises, including the ability to secure their own sponsorship agreements.

Wider Sports News.title: SI hosts masterclass on fan engagement, unveils the Digital Fandom Quadrant
Wider Sports News.summary: SI has launched Digital Fandom Quadrant, a new framework designed to help teams, leagues and federations assess their digital maturity, build stronger direct relationships with fans, and unlock the value of owned first-party data in an AI-driven era. The post SI hosts masterclass on fan engagement, unveils the Digital Fandom Quadrant appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
For too long, Indian sport has treated fan engagement as a synonym for social-media engagement. Followers, views and likes are a starting point and not a very solid one. Teams and leagues broadcast a steady stream of content to reach millions, with little real understanding of who is on the other end. By most estimates, the vast majority of Indian sports organisations cannot identify their individual fans: the data sits on third-party apps and social platforms, owned by those platforms rather than by the organisation itself.

That gap becomes a genuine risk in an AI-driven, personalisation-first era, where an organisation’s fan engagement is only ever as good as the data it owns. This was the premise of a masterclass on the future of fan engagement hosted by Sportz Interactive (SI). The timing is pointed: with the government’s recently approved ₹36,441 crore expansion of the Khelo India programme – the largest public investment in Indian sport since Independence a bid for the 2036 Olympics, and an industry-wide push to build fandom beyond cricket, the question of how organisations actually engage their fans has never mattered more.

The timing is pointed: with the government’s recently approved ₹36,441 crore expansion of the Khelo India programme – the largest public investment in Indian sport since Independence a bid for the 2036 Olympics, and an industry-wide push to build fandom beyond cricket, the question of how organisations actually engage their fans has never mattered more.

Wider Sports News.title: Fourteen Kenyan Stars Selected for Ultimate Sevens Championship
Wider Sports News.summary: Fourteen Kenyan Stars Selected for Ultimate Sevens Championship Kenya Rugby Union
Wider Sports News.body:
Fourteen Kenyan rugby sevens stars have earned selection for the Ultimate Sevens Championship, underlining the country's growing influence on the global sevens stage. The competition, designed to bring together the world's best players,including Olympians and world champions,will be staged across four events in Madrid, Cardiff, Biarritz and London this September.The selected players, drawn from both the Kenya Shujaa and Kenya Lionesses squads, will represent six franchise teams in the new-look championship.

Clan Taran will feature the experienced trio of Vincent Onyala, John Okoth and Sheila Chajira. Onyala heads into the competition as a two-time Olympian who has also represented Kenya at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and the Rugby World Cup Sevens. Okoth, a member of Kenya's Paris 2024 Olympic squad, previously represented Kenya U20 and recently featured in India's Rugby Premier League. Joining them is Kenya Lionesses captain Sheila Chajira, a two-time Olympian who also turned out for the Chennai Bulls in this year's Rugby Premier League.

The post Arsenal’s ‘UK£70m’ extension with Emirates continues England’s most enduring stadium naming rights partnership appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Arsenal and Emirates have agreed a five-year extension to their long-running sponsorship agreement, believed to be worth up to UK£70 million a season. The airline will remain the Premier League champions’ front-of-shirt, training kit and stadium naming rights partner until 2033 in a deal that also covers Arsenal’s women’s and youth teams.

The relationship, which began in 2006, is the longest-running shirt sponsorship in the Premier League. The annual value of this latest extension represents a significant uplift on the previous contract, which is understood to be worth up to UK£50 million annually.

Rugby.body:
The Scarlets have bolstered their front row options ahead of the 2026-2027 United Rugby Championship campaign by signing Moana Pasifika tight-head Chris Apoua. Auckland-born Apoua, 34, who has Samoan heritage, has scored one try in seven appearances for Moana Pasifika and has played for Northland and Southland at provincial level in New Zealand, making his debut a decade ago.

He is Scarlets Director of Rugby Nigel Davies’ eighth signing this summer and joins Wales loosehead Corey Domachowski, who moved from Cardiff when his contract ran out at the end of June.

Rugby.body:
English Prem champions Northampton Saints have appointed Fraser Dingwall as their new club captain. The 27-year-old centre steps into the role after George Furbank's move to Harlequins.

Dingwall, who joined Saints' academy aged 13, has made more than 150 senior appearances and becomes the club's 69th captain since its formation in 1880. "When you look at the list of players who've done it before, it's incredibly special to be part of that group," said the England international, who has won 10 caps since his Test debut in 2024.

The new starting XV features two starting debuts, one in the No.1 jersey for Xavier Numia and one in the No.10 jersey for Josh Jacomb. The Chiefs pivot’s selection comes as Beauden Barrett shifts to fullback, a position he hasn’t played for the All Blacks since he was last in South Africa in 2024.

There’s positive injury news to be found in the front row, too, with acting tour captain Codie Taylor and Tyrel Lomax both overcoming their setbacks to start in what is sure to be a hard-fought set piece battle.

There’s positive injury news to be found in the front row, too, with acting tour captain Codie Taylor and Tyrel Lomax both overcoming their setbacks to start in what is sure to be a hard-fought set piece battle.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: From a $7 note to a national honour: The legacy of Fiji’s Rio 2016 triumph
Rugby.summary: It’s incredible to think that Tuesday only marks ten years to the day since Fiji’s famous victory.
Rugby.body:
While the Rio 2016 winners of the women’s tournament, Australia, can be regarded as one of the most significant teams in the history of the short format, there is one team that serves as a worthy challenger to their legacy: the men’s gold winner from that very same Olympics.

It’s incredible to think that Tuesday only marks ten years to the day since Fiji’s famous victory: because it’s a victory that already feels well-etched into the history of rugby.

Rugby.summary: No selection is set in stone for the All Blacks according to assistant coach Tana Umaga, who is preparing his troops for one final game before the Test series against the Springboks gets underway next week in Johannesburg.
Rugby.body:
No selection is set in stone for the All Blacks according to assistant coach Tana Umaga, who is preparing his troops for one final game before the Test series against the Springboks gets underway next week in Johannesburg.

Umaga and his fellow Kiwi coaches have steered New Zealand to five consecutive victories to begin their 2026 season, albeit the two most recent have come against non-Test sides. But the lesser opposition has presented rare opportunities to experiment with selections while the Stormers and Sharks have still posed stern challenges up front.

Rugby.summary: The injection of Tim Walsh and Reg Tayler into the Wallaroo coaching set up has proven a massive positive for Maddison Levi.
Rugby.body:
The injection of Tim Walsh and Reg Tayler into the Wallaroo coaching set up has proven a massive positive for Maddison Levi, the sevens speedster keen to bring her skillset to XVs after being named in the squad that will travel to New Zealand to face the Black Ferns.

However, one of the key things that Levi aims to bring is the mindset of sevens, and teaching her XVs teammates the ins and outs of what it takes to beat New Zealand. The Wallaroos’ match at Mount Smart Stadium in Auckland will mark their 100th Test match and their 45th in just five years, and that elusive maiden victory over the Black Ferns still awaits from 30 attempts.

Rugby.title: Four Springboks named in Bulls XV to take on All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Johan Ackermann has named four South Africa internationals in his starting Bulls XV to take on the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Johan Ackermann has named four South Africa internationals in his starting Bulls XV to take on the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday. The Bulls boss promised “we’re going to go as strong as we can” this week despite missing a large swathe of players in Rassie Erasmus’s squad, and he has remained true to his word, naming several regular Bulls players alongside the Springboks.

Former Bok Marcell Coetzee will captain the side, and will be joined by 101-cap Springbok Willie le Roux, and Embrose Papier, who earned his first Bok cap in eight years when he started against Scotland in July. Papier will form a half-back partnership with fellow Bok Curwin Bosch, who will mark his return to South Africa after two years in France with Brive.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga receives long-awaited All Blacks call-up
Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga is en route to South Africa to join the All Blacks squad ahead of their game against the Bulls in Pretoria this weekend.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga is en route to South Africa to join the All Blacks squad ahead of their game against the Bulls in Pretoria this weekend. The 32-year-old is three years removed from his last All Blacks cap, which came in New Zealand’s 2023 Rugby World Cup final defeat to the Springboks, having surrendered his All Blacks eligibility when signing with Toshiba Brave Lupus in Japan Rugby League One.

Having now completed that contract and signed with Canterbury, the Crusaders and New Zealand Rugby on an 18-month deal, Mo’unga’s eligibility for national selection was reinstated with his first minutes in the NPC two weeks ago, and will remain until his contract expires after next year’s Rugby World Cup.

Rugby.body:
Yes, two games into their tour to South Africa, the performances have been pretty good. I’m not sure they’ve been pushed too hard by their opponents or we’ve learnt much that we didn’t already know, but there’s definitely not a lot to complain about.

Rugby.title: Canterbury's latest Ranfurly Shield hero describes chaotic Otago win
Rugby.summary: Dominic Gardiner wrote himself into Ranfurly Shield folklore in Canterbury’s successful 19-15 challenge against Otago at Forsyth Barr Stadium in Dunedin on Sunday.
Rugby.body:
Dominic Gardiner wrote himself into Ranfurly Shield folklore in Canterbury’s successful 19-15 challenge against Otago at Forsyth Barr Stadium in Dunedin on Sunday. In the last minute, hard-pressed on defence, Gardiner ripped the ball off Otago replacement hooker Nic Souchon at a ruck. This turnover allowed Canterbury to keep possession until the clock stopped.

“Those turnovers are split-second decisions,” Gardiner told RugbyPass. “I noticed Nic was slightly isolated so I made a grab for the ball, got a cling on it and ripped it away.

Rugby.summary: Saracens' England 'A' centre Angus Hall signs a new contract with the Prem club.
Rugby.body:
Saracens' England 'A' centre Angus Hall has signed a new contract with the Prem club. The 20-year-old, who came through the club's academy, made three Prem appearances last season as well as playing once in the European Champions Cup and three times in the Prem Rugby Cup.

He also spent time on loan at Champ side Ampthill as well as featuring against Spain and an All Blacks XV for England's 'A' side in November. "Angus is exactly the type of player we want to build this club around," newly-appointed director of rugby Brendan Venter told the Saracens website.

He had a breakthrough campaign last year, making 11 first team appearances and featured in four successive Prem games at the tail end of the campaign. "I had a really good taste of first team rugby in big games at the back end of last season and it's made me want even more," he said.

Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson says the partnership with Bedford Blues is "valuable" to both clubs.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson has praised the club's "valuable" partnership with Bedford Blues after an extension of their strategic deal was announced. The agreement, which began in 2020, sees the Prem Rugby and Champ Rugby clubs co-operate on a number of fronts, including the sharing of players and coaches.

Rugby.title: Steve Borthwick makes 5 changes to his 2025/26 Elite Player Squad
Rugby.summary: England have revealed the 25 players who will receive enhanced Elite Player Squad contracts ahead of the new season, with five changes made in total.
Rugby.body:
England have revealed the 25 players who will receive enhanced Elite Player Squad contracts ahead of the new season, with five changes made in total. The five new additions are Gloucester centre Seb Atkinson, Northampton Saints lock Alex Coles, Sale Sharks prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, Bath flanker Guy Pepper and Leicester Tigers scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet.

These new additions are not exactly like-for-like replacements for the five players who have lost their contracts. While Pepper can be seen as a direct replacement for Ben Curry, who failed to play a game for England last season due to a recurring hamstring issue, as can Atkinson for Ollie Lawrence, who fell out of favour during the Six Nations, the final three changes are not like-for-like.

Rugby.title: 'Say ‘yes’ and figure it out afterwards': How one decision changed Jane Clohessy's life
Rugby.summary: Back in November 2022, not long after Jane Clohessy got off stage with her band, a message arrived on her phone.
Rugby.body:
Back in November 2022, not long after Jane Clohessy got off stage with her band, a message arrived on her phone. It was from former Ireland captain, Niamh Briggs – ‘Any interest coming to a Munster session?’

It was not an immediate ‘yes’ but, from that moment, Clohessy’s life would set off down a different path. The Limerick native hails from a rugby-mad family. Her father is Munster and Ireland legend, Peter Clohessy. Many childhood years were spent in and around stadiums and clubhouses. Born in December 1998, Clohessy would have been too young to clearly recall her dad, ‘The Claw’, chasing down Heineken Cup and Six Nations glory. What remains is that feeling of being embraced by a wider family.

Rugby.title: Five players get first England deals in Borthwick shake-up
Rugby.summary: Asher Opoku-Fordjour, Alex Coles, Guy Pepper, Jack van Poortvliet and Seb Atkinson are handed England central contracts for the first time as Steve Borthwick shakes up his squad.
Rugby.body:
England boss Steve Borthwick has shaken up his centrally contracted squad with just over a year to go until the Rugby World Cup. Borthwick has announced the 25 players who will receive enhanced player contracts, worth around £150,000, for the 2026-27 season.

Handed an elite deal for the first time are prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, lock Alex Coles, flanker Guy Pepper, scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet and centre Seb Atkinson. Flanker Ben Curry, versatile back Elliot Daly, centre Ollie Lawrence and wing Tom Roebuck all miss out on contracts, while France-bound number eight Tom Willis is no longer eligible for England selection.

Rugby.title: Ospreys say WRU plan to cut team is wrong
Rugby.summary: Ospreys respond publicly to WRU plans for the first time with the belief four professional Welsh sides is the way forward.
Rugby.body:
The Ospreys board has told the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) its plan to reduce a professional side is the wrong decision. Welsh rugby's governing body has outlined its plans to cut the number of professional teams from four to three by 2028, with WRU-owned Cardiff and privately-backed Dragons set to be given licences.

That announcement has plunged Scarlets and Ospreys into doubt, with the west licence either being awarded to the Llanelli-based side or their Swansea-based rivals. WRU chiefs have said the process to decide the framework for the final decision will begin in December and finish before the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

Rugby.summary: England's Red Roses are in pre-season training before the upcoming WXV Global Series and have been using the controversial smaller balls.
Rugby.body:
England's women are in Nottingham for pre-season this month before the upcoming WXV Global Series. In the new competition, the Red Roses will take on Australia, Canada and New Zealand on home soil in September before further tests across the Atlantic against Canada again and the USA in October.

The last time we saw the world champions in action they were winning another Six Nations' Grand Slam - so what's new? Head coach John Mitchell spills the beans. World Rugby's new size 4.5 balls - about 3% smaller but the same weight as a regulation size five - will be used for the WXV Global Series and are now in use in the England camp.

Rugby.title: High-scoring sevens star Tshiremba will make Springbok debut against Fiji
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women's Sevens flyer Maria Tshiremba will make her Test debut for South Africa this weekend against the Fijiana XV in Lautoka.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women’s Sevens flyer Maria Tshiremba will make her Test debut for South Africa this weekend against the Fijiana XV in Lautoka. This Saturday the 30-year-old will become the 195th player to run out for the Springbok Women. Tshiremba has scored 64 tries in 20 tournament appearances.

Rugby.title: 'Bit unfair': Bulls boss Johan Ackermann's vow before All Blacks clash
Rugby.summary: Bulls head coach Johan Ackermann has promised he will go as "strong as we can" when naming his side to take on the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Bulls head coach Johan Ackermann has promised he will go as “strong as we can” when naming his side to take on the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday. Following a patchy 38-21 win over the Stormers and an emphatic 54-0 win over the Sharks, Dave Rennie’s side will take on the Bulls this weekend in the third match of their Greatest Rivalry tour and their final match before the first Test against the Springboks.

Despite the United Rugby Championship runners-up only recently returning for preseason, Ackermann has vowed that he will not take this match lightly when it comes to selection.

Rugby.title: One thing Les Kiss will like about his first Wallabies win
Rugby.summary: The new Australia head coach started his tenure with a win, but several areas require improvement before they face Japan again.
Rugby.body:
A new Wallabies era under a new head coach has finally begun, and even if it wasn’t overly convincing, at least it started with a win. Australia’s 35-32 victory over Japan was a whole lot more free-flowing and open in steamy Osaka than their 19-15 win in cold, wet Tokyo last season, but the contest left us in the odd situation where both teams will head into Saturday’s return leg in Townsville with a good degree of confidence.

The first encounter was an entertaining game to watch, frustratingly so at times for Wallabies fans, and it really sets up a mouth-watering contest this weekend. While Les Kiss and his coaching team will take positives from the three-point win, there were also more than a few things that need some urgent attention this week.

Rugby.title: Nonu performs solo haka in response to All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks star Ma'a Nonu responds to the haka by performing one of his own before his club side's game with New Zealanders in Durban.
Rugby.body:
New Zealand rugby union great Ma'a Nonu performed a solo haka in response to the All Blacks' haka before his Sharks side fell to a heavy defeat in Durban. The All Blacks continued their tour of South Africa with a resounding 54-0 victory, though what happened pre-match will go down in rugby folklore.

After New Zealand performed their usual Ka Mate haka, Nonu stepped in front of his Sharks team-mates and responded with Kapa o Pango, the All Blacks' alternative haka. The 44-year-old played 104 matches for New Zealand between 2003 and 2015, and was part of the side that won the Rugby World Cup in 2011 and 2015.

Rugby.title: Former England coach Brian Smith dies aged 59
Rugby.summary: Former England assistant coach Brian Smith has died at the 59 after a battle with an aggressive cancer.
Rugby.body:
Former England assistant coach Brian Smith has died at the 59 after a battle with an aggressive cancer. Dr Ian PM Lambert, principal Scots College where Smith had worked since 2015, confirmed his death on Wednesday.

The former fly-half made six appearances for Australia, including three at the 1987 Rugby World Cup, before earning nine caps for Ireland while studying at Oxford University. Upon his return to Australia, Smith made the move to rugby league, where he made 43 NRL appearances across four seasons for the Balmain Tigers and Eastern Suburbs.

Rugby.title: 10 years on: Remembering Fiji’s historic gold at Rio Olympics
Rugby.summary: It’s been 10 years since one of the most famous days in rugby sevens history, when Fiji defeated Great Britain 43-7 to win Olympic gold.
Rugby.body:
It’s been 10 years since one of the most famous days in rugby sevens history, when Fiji defeated Great Britain 43-7 to win Olympic gold in Rio. The 2016 Rio Summer Games marked the return of rugby union to the Olympic stage, and the first time sevens had been on show.

Rugby had been held at the Olympics four times before, with the USA going back-to-back with gold medals in 1920 and 1924, and France collected silver on those two occasions. But the sport didn’t return to the Olympics, in any format, for more than 90 years.

Rugby.title: Ethan de Groot makes 'easy' call on future with new deal until 2029
Rugby.summary: The deal's announcement comes just hours after De Groot suited up for a non-Test match against the Sharks in Durban, playing 54 minutes in the 54-0 win.
Rugby.body:
Ethan de Groot has re-committed his future to New Zealand Rugby, the Highlanders and Southland until 2029. The move will ensure the loosehead prop’s eligibility at the time of the next British and Irish Lions Tour of New Zealand, with the opportunity to add to his 43-Test tally in the meantime, including at next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The deal’s announcement comes just hours after De Groot suited up for a non-Test match against the Sharks in Durban, playing 54 minutes in the 54-0 win. He cited the arrival of his first child, Nova, as a major reason to stick around, even though overseas offers were undoubtedly on the table.

Rugby.title: Rugby sevens pools confirmed for Dakar Summer Youth Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: After making its debut at the 2014 iteration in Nanjing, rugby sevens is set to return to the Youth Olympic Games format.
Rugby.body:
After making its debut at the 2014 iteration in Nanjing, rugby sevens is set to return to the Youth Olympic Games format, as 16 teams and 15 nations have been confirmed to feature at the 2026 Dakar event in November this year.

Around 2700 young athletes are expected to compete across 25 competition sports, with over 120 nations set to be represented, marking the first time ever an Olympic Games of any kind has ever been played on the African continent.

Rugby.title: Seven clips the Wallabies will be analysing after another tight win over Japan
Rugby.summary: Let’s be blunt: seven linebreaks is far too many, and so is the total of nine the Japanese managed to get against the Wallabies, according to the stats.
Rugby.body:
Let’s be blunt: seven linebreaks is far too many, and so is the total of nine the Japanese managed to get against the Wallabies, according to the stats. It was the first look at new defence coach Scott McLeod’s defensive system, and it was every bit as aggressive as head coach Les Kiss had foreshadowed during the week, saying he wanted to “attack” with defence.

While nine linebreaks were recorded, seven of them will likely feature heavily in review this week for the Wallabies. It will be embarrassing watching for some, frustrating for others, with varying degrees of complexity in solving the issues.

Rugby.title: Aseza Hele: 'You don't know how much you will miss that jersey'
Rugby.summary: Aseza Hele had a long wait between her 32nd and 33rd Test caps for the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Aseza Hele had a long wait between her 32nd and 33rd Test caps for the Springbok Women. Before last weekend’s 55-12 win over the Fijiana XV in Suva, the last time the back-row wore a green and gold jersey was in the team’s quarter-final exit against the Black Ferns at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

Rugby.title: Ulster reveal summer surgery to Henderson alongside three team-mates

Rugby.body:
Ulster have confirmed that captain Iain Henderson will be out of action for a “number of months” after undergoing an operation on his hip this summer. While the procedure was a success, the 34-year-old will nevertheless be sidelined for the start of the season, which begins on September 25 for Ulster with a visit from Edinburgh in the United Rugby Championship.

The 85-cap international is one of four players who have gone under the knife during the offseason, with fellow Ireland representative Bryn Ward also part of that list. The 22-year-old made his debut for Andy Farrell’s side in July against Japan, but has since had his shoulder operated on.

Rugby.title: Why Rassie will be happier than Rennie with early omens of Greatest Rivalry tour
Rugby.summary: A stop-start, set-piece-based game like the Stormers tour opener will not suit the All Blacks if the pattern extends into the Test series.
Rugby.body:
The intensity is back, the novelty is back. The Greatest Rivalry in rugby is finally back on the rails. The novelty has been given a huge helping hand by South Africa’s abandonment of Super Rugby and move towards northern domestic competitions. The players no longer experience the ho-hum staleness of the over-familiar. The razor-edge intensity has been merely dormant, awaiting the time to wake up like a vengeful ghost summoned on some unwitting rugby Ouija board.

The 47,130 baying fans at the DHL Stadium in Cape Town will eagerly testify to both. It was a portentous occasion with meaningful bite, and in the course of the 80 minutes Springboks supremo Rassie Erasmus drew rather more blood than his counterpart Dave Rennie. The All Blacks beat the Stormers comfortably enough in the end, 38-21 and six tries to three, but the game was played out under rules which will suit South Africa rather more than New Zealand, if the early omens extend as far as the Test series which begins on 22 August at Ellis Park.

Rugby.title: Bath in 'serious discussions' to play in Reading
Rugby.summary: Reading owner Rob Couhig says the club have had "serious discussions" with Bath about the Prem Rugby club playing at their stadium.
Rugby.body:
Bath have had "serious discussions" about playing two of their 2026-27 games at Reading's Select Car Leasing Stadium, Royals owner Rob Couhig has said. Bath confirmed they will play their final two home games of the Prem season away from the Recreation Ground to enable construction work to begin as part of a redevelopment.

Couhig, who took over as Reading owner in May 2025, said the League One club have had talks with Bath but would not disclose how far they have progressed. "The stadium is well equipped for it, they would be foolish to not try and pursue us," the American told BBC Radio Berkshire.

Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has predicted that Rassie Erasmus will start Manie Libbok at fly-half for the Springboks' first match against...
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has predicted that Rassie Erasmus will start Manie Libbok at fly-half for the Springboks’ first match against the All Blacks in the Greatest Rivalry, but would prefer to see Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu there.

South Africa’s first Test with the All Blacks gets underway in less than two weeks at Ellis Park, with no certainty as to who Erasmus will select at fly-half, or many other positions, for that matter, given the depth the world champions have across the field.

Rugby.title: 'The opportunity for growth is enormous': Fukofuka lands new coaching role after Scotland exit
Rugby.summary: Eight days after his exit as Scotland head coach Sione Fukofuka has been appointed head coach of the Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
Eight days after his exit as Scotland head coach Sione Fukofuka has been appointed head coach of the Wallaroos. The 47-year-old left his role with Scotland after nearly eight months under compassionate grounds and cited ‘family stress’ as a reason for his departure from the position.

Across his five matches in charge of Scotland at the Guinness Women’s Six Nations, Fukofuka presided over one win against Wales at the beginning of the Championship. In addition to his tenure with Scotland, Fukofuka also spent time as head coach of the USA Women’s Eagles for two and a half years – who he led at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 – and spent three years as an assistant coach with the Wallaroos.

Rugby.summary: With Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 already far gone in the rear window mirror, the Yaras have, for the last two months, quietly adjusted and tweaked themselves ahead of the WXV Global Series Challenger.
Rugby.body:
With Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 already far gone in the rear window mirror, the Yaras have, for the last two months, quietly adjusted and tweaked themselves ahead of the WXV Global Series Challenger.

Now under the guidance of Guilherme Coghetto, recently appointed head coach of Brazil’s women’s national team, the Yaras are looking to the future, as he explains. “The 2025 World Cup will always be a wonderful moment in our history, but we need to look forward and keep growing. If we want to win a game in a World Cup, we need to be more competitive, and for that the team needs to increase its output, be it physical, technical and psychological.”

Rugby.title: 'The phoney war on the Greatest Rivalry tour is already gale-force in its intensity.'
Rugby.summary: A clash of styles is at the heart of The Greatest Rivalry and whoever prevails will set the tone for the short-term future of rugby
Rugby.body:
Are you sitting comfortably? Then I’ll begin with a story from a different era of rugby over 40 years ago, well before the advent of professionalism. A well-known, but highly-respected referee had just finished managing a Five Nations match between England and Ireland, in which he had kept the game flowing and penalized only the offences which were absolutely necessary.

At the dinner after the game, England captain and future World Rugby chair Bill Beaumont got up to speak: “I don’t normally do this… but I want to start by complimenting the referee for an exceptional performance. He was the best man on the field by far, and he deserved the man-of-the match award.” Cue a few guffaws from the suits. It was one of many pats on the back the official received after the game, from players and coaches alike.

Rugby.summary: Declan Meredith hasn’t been overawed by the chance to play alongside some giants of Australian rugby, having become a well-respected member of the group.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies prop Allan Alaalatoa has played 92 Tests and Rob Valetini is a two-time recipient of the John Eales Medal. But Declan Meredith hasn’t been overawed by the chance to play alongside some giants of Australian rugby, having become a well-respected member of the group.

Rugby.title: 'Vulnerable': Steve Hansen warns Springboks over risky bench tactic
Rugby.summary: “I hear the commentators, ‘it’s changed the course of the game’, but you know that before you go in, I don’t think you can use it as an excuse for anything.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks head coach Steve Hansen has used the Stormers’ six-two split outcome as a warning to Rassie Erasmus and the Springboks ahead of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry. Hansen’s claim follows the Stormers’ early injuries to halfbacks Imad Khan and Dewaldt Duvenage against the All Blacks, leaving their only bench back replacement, Wandisile Simelane, and the other outside-backs to monitor the base of the ruck.

Stormers head coach John Dobson opted for the popular six-two split on the bench, carrying an extra forward to provide impact and versatility against the All Blacks. The tactic, used often at Test level by Erasmus and other Test sides, can work in the team’s advantage if everything goes to plan, and no backline players, or only one, get injured during the 80-minute contest.

Rugby.title: Wallabies lock Miles Amatosero cops suspension for dangerous ruck entry
Rugby.summary: "Amatosero was given permission to apply to take part in World Rugby's Coaching Intervention Programme as a substitute for the final match of the sanction."
Rugby.body:
Wallabies and Waratahs lock Miles Amatosero has copped a suspension for a dangerous ruck entry against Japan in Osaka. Amatosero was yellow-carded in the 33rd minute of Les Kiss’ first outing as head coach of the Wallabies for a high shot on a Japanese player at a breakdown.

Referee Eoghan Cross initially sent the lock to the sin bin before the yellow card turned red, ruling the Waratahs enforcer out of the rest of the contest. The Wallabies overcame a valiant effort from Eddie Jones’ Brave Blossoms, helped by second-half scores from Max Jorgensen, Fraser McReight, and Taniela Tupou.

Rugby.summary: Debate over the best position for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii is the "first world problem" new Wallabies coach Les Kiss will attempt to solve in a Japan rematch in Townsville.
Rugby.body:
Debate over the best position for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii is the “first world problem” new Wallabies coach Les Kiss will attempt to solve in a Japan rematch in Townsville. With Len Ikitau (ankle) injured, Suaalii and Hunter Paisami formed the midfield partnership in Australia’s hard-fought 35-32 defeat of Japan in Osaka on Saturday.

No.12 Paisami, coached by Kiss at the Queensland Reds for the last three seasons, made the most of his call-up as one of the side’s best starters alongside impressive lock Josh Canham.

Rugby.title: Why Dave Rennie handed Luke Jacobson the All Blacks captaincy
Rugby.summary: "Looking forward to getting out there and to be honest, trying not to think about too deeply. Probably take the time after the game to just appreciate it."
Rugby.body:
It was all surprises when Dave Rennie read out the 23 names that would take on the Sharks in Durban, especially for Luke Jacobson, who was selected to captain the All Blacks for the first time.

The Chiefs captain led the New Zealand U20s to their last World Cup title back in 2017, but has never had the chance to lead the All Blacks in his 27 Test caps. On Wednesday morning NZT, against the Sharks in Durban, Jacobson will lead the All Blacks in the side’s second match on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour for 2026.

Rugby.body:

The 25-year-old hasn’t featured in Super Rugby Pacific since 2023, with Moana Pasifika against the Hurricanes, but has played for Auckland, Counties Manukau, and Hawke’s Bay in the Hilux NPC competition.

Rugby.title: Gloucester decide against Villa Park return
Rugby.summary: Gloucester Rugby confirm they will not be returning to Villa Park to face Leicester Tigers in the Prem next season.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester have ditched plans to again stage next season's Prem match against Leicester Tigers at Villa Park. The club's home Slater Cup fixture was taken on the road to the home of Premier League side Aston Villa for the first time last season and drew an attendance of 24,298 as the Tigers won 36-17.

However Gloucester have decided to return to Kingsholm - which has a capacity of 16,000 - for next season's game on the weekend of 27 March, 2027. The club said the decision had been influenced by significant stadium developments planned at Villa Park over the coming months.

Rugby.title: All Blacks remove Cam Roigard from Sharks game as 'precautionary measure'
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks have removed star halfback Cam Roigard from this week's Sharks game as a "precautionary measure", noting a tight calf as the cause for concern.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have removed star halfback Cam Roigard from this week’s Sharks game as a “precautionary measure”, noting a tight calf as the cause for concern. Roigard was named on the bench for the Sharks contest after missing the opening match of the tour, but will now be replaced in the No.21 jersey by Cortez Ratima, with Kyle Preston remaining in the starting unit for his first start in the black jersey.

The Hurricanes star had a heavy workload throughout the opening block of Nations Championship games, starting all three Tests and averaging just shy of 70 minutes per game. The game time saw him emerge from the July Tests with the most passes, carries, defenders beaten and tries of any halfback in the 12-team tournament.

Rugby.summary: Hanekom delivered a man-of-the-match performance in his second showing of the year after missing the entire 2025 season with injury.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has shot down the suggestion that there will be competition for the No.8 jersey after Cameron Hanekom’s display in Argentina. Hanekom delivered a man-of-the-match performance in his second showing of the year after missing the entire 2025 season with injury.

The 24-year-old has been a standout in the URC for the Bulls for a number of years but injuries have limited his international career to just three caps. The performance raised eyebrows for many with incumbent No.8 Jasper Wiese was left back in South Africa to prepare for the series against the All Blacks.

Rugby.title: 54th Mercantile Rugby Sevens
Rugby.summary: 54th Mercantile Rugby Sevens The Morning
Rugby.body:
The Mercantile Rugby Football Association (MRFA) has announced that the 54th Mercantile Rugby Sevens will be held from 13 to 15 November, marking the return of one of Sri Lanka’s longest-running and most popular corporate rugby sevens tournaments.

Spanning more than five decades, the Mercantile Rugby Sevens has become a prominent fixture in Sri Lanka’s corporate sporting calendar, known for its competitive spirit, camaraderie and sportsmanship.

Rugby.title: Sale Sharks co-owner makes major claim over future stadium
Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks co-owner Michelle Orange has pledged that the club will be in its own stadium within the next decade, after revealing the limited revenue it can generate from playing at its rented home.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks co-owner Michelle Orange has pledged that the club will be in its own stadium within the next decade, after revealing the limited revenue it can generate from playing at its rented home.

Orange told the Love of Rugby podcast that the club has to pay the owners of the CorpAcq Stadium, Salford City Council, six per cent of every ticket sold, but doesn’t earn revenue from sources such as car parking or food and drink.

Rugby.title: Bath to go on the road for Prem season run-in
Rugby.summary: Bath's last two home games of the season to be played away from The Rec as part of an accelerated construction plan for the club's new stadium.
Rugby.body:
Bath's last two home games of the season will be played away from The Rec as part of an accelerated construction plan for the club's new stadium. The new timeline, which is aimed at completing the revamped stadium for Bath in time for the start of the 2028-29 season, will see the games against Harlequins on the weekend of 15 May and Saracens on 5 June moved.

Should Bath secure a home semi-final, as they have done for the past three seasons, this will also have to be taken on the road. "We are in discussion with alternative host venues, and we will update you once the location for these fixtures is confirmed," Bath chief executive Tarquin McDonald wrote in an open letter to club supporters, external.

Rugby.summary: A 36-player Las Leonas squad has been named as preparations for the WXV Global Series Challenger commence.
Rugby.body:
A 36-player Las Leonas squad has been named as preparations for the WXV Global Series Challenger commence. Regis Sonnes – who led Spain to a Rugby Europe Women’s Championship title in his first campaign as head coach – will see his team play Fiji, Samoa and Brazil across three consecutive weekends in Hong Kong China.

The squad includes scrum-half Anne Fernández de Corres. This season the 28-year-old turned out for the ACT Brumbies in Super Rugby Women’s and claimed the team’s Helen Taylor Award for Women’s Player of the Year at the conclusion of her debut season in Canberra.

Rugby.summary: The Ospreys are closing in on a deal with former Wallaby wing Marika Koroibete, who has been speaking to them about joining ahead of the new United Rugby Championship season...
Rugby.body:
The Ospreys are closing in on a deal with former Wallaby wing Marika Koroibete, who has been speaking to them about joining ahead of the new United Rugby Championship season, which they kick off against the Sharks at Kings Park at the end of next month.

The Ospreys already have two Australian internationals at the club, with Chiefs inside centre Lalakai Foketi joining back-rower Liam Wright in South Wales earlier this summer. They have also signed Lawson Creighton from the Waratahs.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women expressed 'freedom' in big Fijiana win
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women assistant coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt was enthused with the team's 55-12 win against Fiji in Suva on Saturday afternoon.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women assistant coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt was enthused with the team’s 55-12 win against Fiji in Suva on Saturday afternoon. Across the 80 minutes, South Africa scores from Nombuyekezo Mdliki, Lindelwa Gwala, Vainah Ubisi, Sizophila Solontsi, Maceala Samboya, Byrhandre Dolf, Sinelitha Noxeke and a Xoliswa Khuzwayo brace put clear distance between the two teams.

Springbok captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg kicked two conversions, while Dolf converted three tries. Springbok Women Sevens star Shiniqwa Lamprecht made her Test debut as a starter in the contest.

Rugby.summary: Bath Rugby have revealed plans to bring forward the completion of their long-awaited stadium redevelopment, with chief executive Tarquin McDonald...
Rugby.body:
Bath Rugby have revealed plans to bring forward the completion of their long-awaited stadium redevelopment, with chief executive Tarquin McDonald confirming the club has submitted a planning amendment aimed at cutting the construction programme to around 18 months.

Writing in an open letter to supporters, McDonald said the club remains on course to begin construction in 2027 but believes the revised phasing could allow the new stadium to be ready for the start of the 2028/29 season.

Rugby.summary: Ireland and Lions inside-centre Robbie Henshaw could finish his career away from Leinster after being marketed as available for a move following next year’s World Cup in Australia.
Rugby.body:
Ireland and Lions inside-centre Robbie Henshaw could finish his career away from Leinster after being marketed as available for a move following next year’s World Cup in Australia.

Athlone-born Henshaw, who celebrated his 33rd birthday in June, has played over 120 games for Leinster since he joined them from Connacht a decade ago, winning four Pro 14 crowns and a United Rugby Championship title.

Rugby.summary: Wing Lisa Neumann returns from injury as head coach Sean Lynn names 14 uncapped players in a 46-strong squad preparing for four autumn Tests.
Rugby.body:
Wing Lisa Neumann returns for Wales in an extended 46-player training squad preparing for the autumn's four-match WXV Global Series. The 32-year-old, who remains unattached after leaving Harlequins in July, missed almost all of the 2026 Six Nations after suffering a hamstring injury in the opening game against Scotland.

Head coach Sean Lynn has named 14 uncapped players as preparations begin for home games against South Africa and the USA in September, before two away Tests against Japan in October.

Rugby.body:
The Sharks have lost Springbok Vincent Tshituka and second-row Emile van Heerden from their squad for Tuesday’s Greatest Rivalry clash with the All Blacks at Hollywoodbets Kings Park.

The two-cap Tshituka, who made his debut for the world champions against Italy last year, has been ruled out after suffering a reported head injury in training. Van Heerden has also been withdrawn after picking up an injury. The 6’7, 110kg 26-year-old was set to line up against the All Blacks but now Deon Slabbert has been promoted into the starting XV to partner Hendre Stassen.

Rugby.summary: Wales head coach Sean Lynn has named a 46-player extended training squad for their four-game WXV Global Series campaign.
Rugby.body:
Wales head coach Sean Lynn has named a 46-player extended training squad for their four-game WXV Global Series campaign. In total 14 uncapped players have been named in the squad. This includes Lily Hawkins, Amy Williams, Kelsie Webster, Stella Orrin and Lucy Issac, who all represented Wales in their uncapped fixture against the Barbarians at Allianz Stadium in June.

Ffion Williuams, Crystal James, Shanelle Williams and Savannah Picton Powell are more of the uncapped players named in the squad. Of the 46 players selected by Lynn, 37 have played Celtic Challenge rugby for either Brython Thunder or Gwalia Lightning.

Rugby.title: 'I can't wait to get started': Edinburgh appoint ex-Scotland international as new head coach
Rugby.summary: Scotland Under-21 coach Louise Dalgliesh has been appointed head coach of Edinburgh Rugby in the Celtic Challenge.
Rugby.body:
Scotland Under-21 coach Louise Dalgliesh has been appointed head coach of Edinburgh Rugby in the Celtic Challenge. A 67-cap Scotland international during her playing career, she joined the capital side from club partner the University of Edinburgh, where she served as Head of Performance for Women’s Rugby.

Dalgliesh replaces Claire Cruickshank at Edinburgh, who was recently appointed as Scottish Rugby’s first-ever Women’s National Academy Manager. The former Scotland international has worked for Japan Women as an assistant coach at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2021 [hosted in 2022] and as an assistant for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club Sale Sharks. In May 2025 Dalgliesh was appointed head coach of Scotland U20/U21.

Rugby.summary: Nick Mallett has identified three areas South Africa can “definitely get better” in before facing the All Blacks, with the former Springboks...
Rugby.body:
Nick Mallett has identified three areas South Africa can “definitely get better” in before facing the All Blacks, with the former Springboks head coach calling for improvements in their lineout, attack and contestable kicking.

South Africa edged Argentina 17-10 in Buenos Aires on Saturday in their final match before their attention turns to New Zealand and the Greatest Rivalry. The victory at Estadio José Amalfitani was far from flawless, with Los Pumas making life uncomfortable for the world champions for large periods before the visitors eventually secured the win following a nervey final play.

Rugby.title: Rugby union's sniffiness around making money is exhausting
Rugby.summary: There has been a curious sniffiness around Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, as if South Africa and New Zealand have committed some breach of rugby etiquette by discovering...
Rugby.body:
A “branded, fundraising exercise”, according to The Times. The commercial imperatives have been “hammered home”, according to The Guardian. Elsewhere, the phrase “cash grab” has inevitably appeared.

There has been a curious sniffiness around Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, as if South Africa and New Zealand have committed some breach of rugby etiquette by discovering that people might pay good money to watch the two best teams in the world play each other.

Rugby.title: Black Ferns XV name 23-strong squad to battle Black Ferns in Wellington
Rugby.summary: Blair Baxter has included five capped Black Ferns in his Black Ferns XV squad ahead of this weekend's one-off clash.
Rugby.body:
Blair Baxter has included five capped Black Ferns in his Black Ferns XV squad ahead of this weekend’s one-off clash. On Friday afternoon, the Black Ferns XV will take on the Black Ferns at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt, Wellington. Nine players who represented the Black Ferns XV in 2025 have been selected in Whitney Hanson’s Black Ferns squad for upcoming O’Reilly Cup, Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry and WXV Global Series fixtures.

“This is a strong squad that has a balance of talent and potential with a shared ambition of representing the Black Ferns,” Baxter said. “This fixture is a great opportunity for these players to experience what will look and feel like a Test week. It’s also a chance for us to establish a solid foundation for Black Ferns XV as we build towards the first-ever British & Irish Lions Women’s Series next year.”

Rugby.summary: Hunter Paisami is hungry for a hometown farewell as calls mount for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to switch to the wing under new Wallabies coach Les Kiss.
Rugby.body:
Hunter Paisami is hungry for a hometown farewell as calls mount for Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to switch to the wing under new Wallabies coach Les Kiss. With Len Ikitau (ankle) injured, the pair formed the midfield partnership in Australia’s hard-fought 35-32 defeat of Japan in Osaka on Saturday.

Rugby.title: Wallabies won't shy away from 'license to play' under Kiss
Rugby.summary: Australia defied a 20-minute red card and brutal heat and humidity to pip Eddie Jones's plucky Japan 35-32 and ensure the Kiss era began with victory on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies won’t be spooked off the Les Kiss way after avoiding an Osaka disaster, pledging to commit after being “given a licence to play” by the new coach. Australia defied a 20-minute red card and brutal heat and humidity to pip Eddie Jones’s plucky Japan 35-32 and ensure the Kiss era began with victory on Saturday.

Flyhalf Declan Meredith battled all night to make ground with his exit kicks, and the fluency shown in a last-start flogging of Italy wasn’t there. But, after winning just five of 15 Tests under Joe Schmidt last year, they did enough and will meet Japan again in friendlier conditions in Townsville this Saturday afternoon, hoping to find a higher gear.

Rugby.summary: Stormers flanker and Springbok Deon Fourie has been called into the Springboks ahead of the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Stormers flanker and Springbok Deon Fourie has been called into the Springboks ahead of the Greatest Rivalry series according to a report by SA Rugby Mag. The 39-year-old was industrious for the Stormers against the All Blacks on Friday night playing openside flanker and will now potentially take on the Test team.

He provides loose forward and hooker cover for the Springboks who are awaiting scans on captain Siya Kolisi who was forced off the field early in Buenos Aires against Argentina.

Rugby.summary: "Guys like Peter Lakai really fronted up. Fabian Holland, how good was he, having not played a lot of rugby, and equally you can just see the balance of that side and players that hadn't played a lot.
Rugby.body:
Former All Black halfback Justin Marshall believes there are multiple areas of concern for Dave Rennie after their 17-point triumph over the Stormers in Cape Town. Rennie and the All Blacks overcame a physical challenge by the United Rugby Championship side on Saturday morning NZT, where they were put under enormous amounts of pressure on several fronts.

The All Blacks were penalised and yellow-carded on multiple occasions by English referee Karl Dickson, which highlighted areas where Rennie’s side must improve before the four-Test series against the Springboks.

Rugby.summary: “The ball’s in Razor’s court at the moment, but I don’t want to push him or pressure him in any way."
Rugby.body:
The New Zealand Herald has reported that former All Blacks head coach Scott Robertson has been offered an NRL head coaching role with the Southern Orcas. The proposed Christchurch-based NRL franchise, according to club president Sir Graham Lowe, has tabled a four-year deal to Robertson to become the head coach.

The 51-year-old has been without a role since departing the All Blacks frame in January 2026, apart from a short stint with the Barbarians alongside Felipe Contepomi. “We’re well aware that he’s not coached rugby league before, but he’s certainly got a good handle on rugby league and has been looking at it closely and studying it closely for a long time; that’s quite obvious,” Lowe told the Herald.

Hansen’s side will take on the Black Ferns XV this Friday at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt, before beginning to prepare for the O’Reilly Cup presented by Bupa against Australia.

Former Springbok wing Sbu Nkosi has revealed that the death of his two children at birth sat behind the mental health crisis that engulfed his time at the Vodacom Bulls and left him fearing for his own safety.

Nkosi, a member of South Africa’s 2019 Rugby World Cup-winning squad, disappeared from public view in late 2022. The Bulls said he had been absent without leave for three weeks and that their last contact with him had come on November 11, prompting a missing-person case to be opened with the South African Police Service (SAPS).

Rugby.title: Japan vs Wallabies: Dearns and Canham World XV locks, Gordon should start
Rugby.summary: The Wallabies are off to a winning start under new coach Les Kiss, overcoming a Miles Amatosero 20-minute red card in a tense 35-32 win over Japan.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies are off to a winning start under new coach Les Kiss, overcoming a Miles Amatosero 20-minute red card in a tense 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka. It’s the first time in 12 months that the Wallabies have successfully gone back-to-back with wins, following a 47-point triumph over Italy last month. They will chase more drought-breaking history next weekend, having not won three Tests in a row since the July internationals in 2024.

Next up for the Wallabies is another clash with the Brave Blossoms, with Townsville’s Queensland Country Bank Stadium hosting the fixture, 14 months out from Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 on home soil.

Rugby.title: Four major surgeries in four years: Newest Wallaby's hard-earned Osaka debut
Rugby.summary: Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark.
Rugby.body:
Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark after a hard-earned debut in Osaka. Named on the bench, the Queensland Reds centre was made to wait more than 70 minutes before being thrust into the action and then defending furiously in a 35-32 Saturday night defeat of Japan.

The 27-year-old became Wallaby No.999 in the process, the honour coming despite Henry enduring four major surgeries in as many years. “It’s a great number, might have to talk to my wife about getting it tattooed,” said Henry, who has his surname inked on his forearm.

Rugby.summary: Gloucester chairman Martin St Quinton has backed the claims of Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn, who says that England star Henry Pollock is worthy of a £1 million-a-year contract from Northampton Saints.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester chairman Martin St Quinton has backed the claims of Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn, who says that England star Henry Pollock is worthy of a £1 million-a-year contract from Northampton Saints.

St Quinton told Track Radio that Pollock, who is now in the final year of his Saints deal, is worth every penny of £1 million because he is one of the biggest stars in the league but admits that it would be hard for the Gallagher PREM outfit to splash out seven figures.

Rugby.title: Hansen and Jones predict same outcome in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour
Rugby.summary: Both Sir Steve Hansen and Eddie Jones have arrived at the same conclusion when predicting the four-Test section of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Tour, with both coaches expecting a series too tight to call.
Rugby.body:
Both Sir Steve Hansen and Eddie Jones have arrived at the same conclusion when predicting the four-Test section of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, with both coaches expecting a series too tight to call.

The extended nature of the series leaves the door open for a 2-2 finish, but details of the official tiebreaker scenarios are yet to be confirmed. Hansen, the 2015 Rugby World Cup-winning All Blacks coach, and Jones, the man who ended his title defence campaign in a famous 2019 semi-final while in charge of England, were asked for their verdicts on the Rugby Unity podcast, with Hansen pondering: “Four Tests, probably two-all.”

Rugby.title: 10th anniversary: The lasting legacy of Australia’s Rio 2016 golden girls
Rugby.summary: Olympic heroes from the gold medal-winning Australian rugby sevens team walked out onto the field at Sydney’s Allianz Stadium on Friday.
Rugby.body:
Olympic heroes from the gold medal-winning Australian rugby sevens team walked onto the field at Sydney’s Allianz Stadium on Friday, one day before the 10th anniversary of their historic 24-17 win over New Zealand at Rio de Janeiro’s Deodoro Stadium.

The rugby sevens ‘golden girls’ were among Australia’s history makers in Rio, with the nation claiming eight gold across those Games. Charlotte Caslick raced away for a crucial try with five minutes left, as the Aussies raced out to a 17-point lead.

Rugby.title: 'Hell of a player': Dave Rennie on his two All Blacks debutants and rising star
Rugby.summary: The opening match of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour saw two new faces wear the black jersey for the first time, and plenty more return to it after spells away.
Rugby.body:
The opening match of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour saw two new faces wear the black jersey for the first time, and plenty more return to it after spells away. While they won’t be awarded Test caps, Josh Jacomb replaced Beauden Barrett in the 68th minute and injected some life into the attack, and Siale Lauakai came on for Pasilio Tosi after 47 minutes and was quickly subjected to the power of the Stormers’ scrum, which had the upper hand all night.

While the game was largely a dead heat for the first hour, the New Zealand bench sparked a late surge that ultimately saw the visitors emerge as 17-point victors. The debutants contributed to that surge, and head coach Dave Rennie recognised the occasion as a special one for both players.

Rugby.title: Patrick Tuipulotu reflects on All Blacks' 'mistakes' in Stormers clash
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie's side lost 15 turnovers in Cape Town, and missed 20 tackles, highlighting how difficult the Stormers were to break down.
Rugby.body:
Stand-in All Blacks captain Patrick Tuipulotu has reflected on their 17-point victory at DHL Stadium over the Stormers, where the visitors received three yellow cards. Anton Lienert-Brown, Simon Parker, and Josh Moorby were all sent to the bin by English referee Karl Dickson, with the All Blacks going down to 13 men at one stage in the first half.

Lienert-Brown was pinged for a high tackle during the first half, Parker infringed during a Stormers lineout drive, and Moorby looked to have stopped a Stormers try on the line, cynically.

Rugby.title: Ma'a Nonu named to face All Blacks in Sharks debut
Rugby.summary: In one of the more unlikely twists in rugby history, New Zealand legend Ma'a Nonu has been named to square off with the All Blacks in his Sharks debut next week.
Rugby.body:
In one of the more unlikely twists in rugby history, New Zealand legend Ma’a Nonu has been named to square off with the All Blacks in his Sharks debut next week. The midweek fixture is the second of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, and will pit one of New Zealand’s all-time greats against the team he played 103 Tests for and won two Rugby World Cups with, as Nonu enters his 25th season as a professional rugby player.

The remarkable story comes just days after Nonu joined the club in person, having signed in a “high-performance mentorship” capacity in late July. The 44-year-old will come off the bench, with Murray Koster named to start at inside centre and rising star Jurenzo Julius in the No.13 jersey.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie addresses All Blacks' three obvious problems in Stormers win
Rugby.summary: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has emerged from the first game of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour happy with his team's character, but disappointed with their discipline and how they fared in the scrum.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has emerged from the first game of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour happy with his team’s character, but disappointed with their discipline, aerial ability, and how they fared in the scrum.

New Zealand was penalised 16 times in the game, many of them in the opening half, resulting in back-to-back yellow cards in just the 11th and 12th minutes. A third yellow was shown in the 77th minute, by which time a flurry of late New Zealand tries had put the game beyond reach.

Rugby.title: The Rio legacy: Why Aussie rugby sevens gold will forever have an impact
Rugby.summary: The Rio legacy: Why Aussie rugby sevens gold will forever have an impact ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
Rugby.body:
Shannon Parry was on a morning jog in Brisbane a few years back when she was stopped in her tracks. Running past a primary school, she noticed a group of girls, aged no more than eight years old, playing rugby.

As the co-captain of Australia's victorious women's rugby sevens team at the 2016 Olympics, Parry was struck by the sight. Parry didn't start playing rugby until she was 18 because the opportunities to do so weren't as readily available when she was younger.

Rugby.summary: Stormers player ratings: Anyone who thought the Stormers would just roll over for the All Blacks was sorely disappointed. The Cape side put...
Rugby.body:

The Cape side put huge pressure on New Zealand’s set-piece in slippery conditions in Cape Town and gave as good as they got during a fiercely competitive first half. While the All Blacks eventually pulled away, the Stormers front row, lineout and a handful of emerging stars made sure this was anything but a procession against one of world rugby’s most decorated sides.

A slew of late tries for the All Blacks put some polish on the 38-21 scoreboard, but this was anything but easy. Part of a Stormers scrum that caused the All Blacks plenty of discomfort throughout his 45-minute shift. Matongo and Neethling Fouche consistently asked questions at scrum time, although they occasionally strayed onto the wrong side of Karl Dickson’s interpretation. A busy outing against high-quality opposition.

Rugby.title: Rugby World Cup team remove head coach 14 months out from tournament
Rugby.summary: Uruguay head coach Rodolfo Ambrosio and assistant coach Juan Figallo have lost their jobs just over one year out from Rugby World Cup 2027.
Rugby.body:
Uruguay head coach Rodolfo Ambrosio and assistant coach Juan Figallo have lost their jobs just over one year out from Rugby World Cup 2027. Following a disappointing opening month in the World Rugby Nations Cup, in which the team won only one game, the board reviewed the work of Ambrosio and Figallo, and both parties agreed to part ways.

Ambrosio, who had previously held the Brazilian Tupís head coach position, joined Uruguay in 2024 after Esteban Meneses opted not to extend his stay after more than a decade working with the Teros.

Rugby.title: Top 14 loosens salary cap ahead of new season
Rugby.summary: The Top 14 is set to introduce a slight financial relaxation of its Salary Cap for the 2026/27 season, which gets underway in a few weeks.
Rugby.body:
The Top 14 is set to introduce a slight financial relaxation of its Salary Cap for the 2026/27 season, which gets underway in a few weeks. The salary ceiling, which limits the total amount a club can devote to player and staff remuneration, will rise from €10.7 million to €11 million. It will then increase by €100,000 per season until it reaches €11.3 million in 2029/30.

This move further widens the financial gap between the French top flight and the Gallagher Premiership. The Premiership’s salary cap sits at £6.4 million (approximately €7.5 million) and will remain unchanged for the 2026/27 campaign, which kicks off on September 25.

Rugby.summary: Les Kiss has made two points very clear at the beginning of his tenure as Wallabies coach: he wants his team to go forward and win collisions, and he wants a competitive environment for positions at all times.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss has made two points very clear at the beginning of his tenure as Wallabies coach: he wants his team to go forward and win collisions, and he wants a competitive environment for positions at all times.

Rugby.title: Brayden Iose on Hurricanes' 'perfect storm', Aaron Smith and Manawatu royalty
Rugby.summary: On August 28, Manawatu officially marks its 140th Anniversary with a special dinner at Central Energy Trust Arena in Palmerston North.
Rugby.body:
On August 28, Manawatu officially marks its 140th Anniversary with a special dinner at Central Energy Trust Arena in Palmerston North. For the last decade, or seven per cent of the Union’s existence, Brayden Iose has been a vital part of the furniture.

The strapping loose forward debuted in a 25-20 win against Southland on September 30, 2017, in Invercargill, a year after captaining the New Zealand Secondary Schools. He has since made 56 appearances for the Turbos, winning the Manawatu Player of the Year award three times. In 2019 he scored a try in the famous 32-29 win against Canterbury in Christchurch, Nick Croswell’s 100th game.

Rugby.title: Blues lure another rising talent north from Highlanders
Rugby.summary: The youngster ended his rookie Super Rugby Pacific campaign with three starts, including a try on debut, after replacing the injured Dylan Pledger during pre-season.
Rugby.body:
The Blues have signed halfback Nic Shearer for the 2027 season, luring the 23-year-old north after a stellar rookie season with the Highlanders. The signing comes after the Blues announced the recruitment of Otago and Highlanders first-five Cam Millar last month, plugging the impending gap to be left by Stephen Perofeta when the All Black makes the move to Japan later this year.

The Blues have also recently re-signed halfback Taufa Funaki, while both Finlay Christie and Sam Nock are off contract at the end of this year. Shearer, who had two seasons of NPC under his belt, one for Canterbury and one for Southland, when he made his Super Rugby debut this March, said he was thrilled to be heading to the City of Sails to be a part of incoming head coach Jason Holland’s game plan.

Rugby.title: As All Blacks fans ramp up for Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, it would be foolhardy to overlook the NPC
Rugby.summary: While all eyes will inevitably be on South Africa for Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, the NPC will be playing out and it has never been more vital
Rugby.body:
They say, when you meet a new baby in the extended family, it’s poor form to ignore any older siblings in the process of making a spirited dash for the latest arrival. It’s a piece of advice that springs to mind seeing how New Zealand Rugby [NZR] has directed all the media attention at the All Blacks’ tour of South Africa – with the national team jetting off from Auckland on the same day that the National Provincial Championship began.

This is certainly a case of the older sibling being overlooked for the agreeable new arrival, and while there were endless stories and opinion pieces about the All Blacks, there was barely a mention of the fact that Waikato had beaten Bay of Plenty in the opening game of what is now called the Hilux NPC.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper Has the World in His Sights: "My Tennis Hasn’t Gone Anywhere”
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper Has the World in His Sights: "My Tennis Hasn’t Gone Anywhere” Esquire
Tennis.body:
This month, Jack Draper hopes to compete at the US Open. The journey to this point has been eventful: in the spring, he announced that Andy Murray would be joining his coaching team, though the 24-year-old  later had to withdraw from Wimbledon because of a recurrent arm injury. In this profile, from our July/August issue, the latest cover star of Esquire Edge discusses his tumultuous past year, teaming up with Murray and his enviable fashion credentials.

Jack Draper is, as far as I’m aware, the only man to have ever performed a body-popping routine on a Wimbledon show court. The occasion was the 2018 boys singles final, and it was the first time I saw Draper — then a slim, rangy 16-year-old — strike a tennis ball. Naturally right-handed, he played as a leftie and seemed to crush forehands off both sides. But it was his swagger that stayed with me, and probably many of the 10,000 spectators on Wimbledon’s Court One. He didn’t win the title, against Taiwanese top seed Tseng Chun-hsin, but the body-popping — busted out after Draper theatrically saved a match point — suggested he was very much at home at the world’s most famous tennis tournament.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper: I cried because I have he had hit rock bottom
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper: I cried because I have he had hit rock bottom The Telegraph
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper said his on-court breakdown as he attempted yet another comeback to the tennis tour was because he had “hit rock bottom”. Draper will be in action on Thursday in the opening round of the Cincinnati Masters as he attempts to continue his return from a long-term injury to his racket arm. Last week, in his first match since Eastbourne, Draper wept for an entire changeover in his three-set defeat by Terence Atmane at the Canadian Open.

It was his first appearance for almost six weeks as a result of the ongoing problems with his left arm, which have affected him since spring last year, and he has admitted that he “did not recognise the player out on court”, thus prompting the sudden outpouring of emotion.

Tennis.title: 'I have to start again' - Draper ready for comeback after hitting 'rock bottom'
Tennis.summary: 'I have to start again' - Draper ready for comeback after hitting 'rock bottom' TNT Sports
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper says he feels like he has hit ”rock bottom” this summer but is ready to "start again" as he explained his tearful reaction during his recent first-round Canadian Open defeat. The former British No. 1 has struggled with a persistent arm injury over the last year, sidelining him for long periods.

Draper's ranking dropped as low as No. 160, having reached world No. 4 in 2025, the year he won a maiden ATP Masters 1000 title at Indian Wells. The 24-year-old returned to the court in Montreal this month for his first appearance since June, but he appeared to suffer from recurring discomfort and ultimately lost 6-3 2-6 6-2 against Terence Atmane.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper: ‘When you reach rock bottom like that you can come back up again’
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper: ‘When you reach rock bottom like that you can come back up again’ The Guardian
Tennis.body:
Those painful images have relentlessly spread to all corners of the internet. Deep in the final set of the first-round match at the Canadian Open against Térence Atmane just over a week ago, 15 months of pent up emotion erupted. Two games from defeat, Draper spent the entire changeover in tears.

This was a devastating and alarming sight. Injuries had already defined so much of Draper’s career, but the uncertainty of trying to recover from a bone bruise injury to his left arm over the past year has been more challenging than anything he has experienced. All of his efforts since last July have been focused on trying to find a way to compete consistently at the highest level again, to no avail.

Tennis.title: Rybakina comeback knocks Osaka out of Canadian Open
Tennis.summary: Elena Rybakina comes back from a set and a break down to beat Naomi Osaka in three sets in their Canadian Open quarter-final.
Tennis.body:
Elena Rybakina came back from a set and a break down to beat Naomi Osaka in three sets in their Canadian Open quarter-final. Four-time Grand Slam winner Osaka had won the first set and was 4-2 up in the second before her Kazakh rival came back to win 4-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 in two hours and 33 minutes.

"I was just trying to fight," said Rybakina, whose 72 unforced errors were her most in a match this season. "The first game was really tough because it cost me the set, and then in the second I was just trying to stay closer to the score, even if I'm losing. I'm super happy that I won this match."

Tennis.body:
World number one Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from this week's Cincinnati Open because of a knee injury, but still expects to be fit for the US Open later this month. The 24-year-old Italian won his fifth Grand Slam singles title by beating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final last month, but has not played since.

"After consulting with my doctors and my team, I have to announce that I need to withdraw from the Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati," Sinner said. "My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept I'm not ready to compete yet.

Tennis.body:
Jack Draper will return to action at the Cincinnati Open next week despite the emotional scenes that followed his latest injury setback at the Canadian Open in Montreal. The British player left the court in tears after his first match since June, raising concerns about whether his US Open preparations had suffered another major blow.

The 24-year-old was making his comeback in Canada after a recurrence of the bone bruising that had previously kept him sidelined for almost seven months. Draper struggled physically during his match against Terence Atmane and eventually appeared unable to continue at his usual level, but the latest update suggests he will not need another extended absence from competition.

Golf.title: How Fat Perez and online creators are cashing in on golf's digital boom
Golf.summary: An online explosion has brought golf, in one form or another, to millions of new fans — and minted a new breed of celebrity in the process. The post How Fat Perez and online creators are cashing in on golf’s digital boom appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Before he lost 100 pounds and gained a million followers, Nick Stubbe was a beefy ex-collegiate golfer with an office job and an Instagram account on which he rarely posted. Weekdays, he worked as an accountant. Weekends, he knocked it around with friends on a rota of courses in Richmond, Va.

The routine suited the easygoing Stubbe, who liked his colleagues and loved his golf, playing to scratch with a buttery swing and a beer-league body that made him look as if he’d stumbled to the first tee from a tailgate. What he didn’t look like was a budding social media star, which was fine by him because he wasn’t trying to become one. The sponsorship deals, celebrity pro-ams, viral videos with Bryson DeChambeau — none of that was part of any plan because, well, there was no plan.
