Golf.title: Golfer admits 'stupidity' after faking hole-in-one
Golf.summary: An amateur golfer says he has "completely made a fool" of himself after admitting he faked making a hole-in-one at a tournament in the United States.
Golf.body:
An amateur golfer says he has "completely made a fool" of himself after admitting he faked making a hole-in-one at a tournament in the United States. Zach Holland was due to play in a two-person team competition at WingHaven Country Club in Missouri when he fraudulently placed the ball in the cup at the fourth hole earlier in the morning, before his round.

Holland, who is a plus-two handicap, had completed the first three holes when he told his group he was going to have to take a phone call as his grandmother was ill, so he would run ahead to the next tee and hit his shot first to keep up with the pace of play.

Golf.title: LIV Golf stars face career ultimatum after DP World Tour snub
Golf.summary: LIV Golf stars face career ultimatum after DP World Tour snub Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour will start imposing fines on LIV Golf players again next season in a move that will serve some of the league’s biggest stars with a career ultimatum. As first reported by The Athletic, the DP World Tour has now informed players it will resume the suspensions and fines that have been handed out for violating the circuit’s conflicting events rules.

The European circuit struck a deal with eight LIV golfers in February to participate in the breakaway league’s events without incurring such punishments. In return, the octet of players agreed to settle all previous fines, drop appeals, as well as participating in an extra number of DP World Tour events.

Golf.body:

He’s hardly the only one who’s fallen for the place. Merion has that effect on people. Hugh Wilson’s design in the leafy suburbs of Philadelphia — this week’s host of the U.S. Amateur Championship — has long been an architectural darling and a fixture on Top 100 lists (it sits at No. 13 on GOLF’s current global ranking).

Golf.body:
Tickets for LIV Golf's season-ending Team Championship event in Michigan are no longer on sale on its official website amid reports it has been cancelled. The Telegraph reported on Wednesday that LIV's players had been told that the lucrative Team Championship event, scheduled to take place in Michigan in two weeks' time, had been cancelled.

At that point, tickets were still being advertised for sale on LIV's website but that was no longer the case as of Thursday morning. A message on the pages where tickets had been available, for both grounds and hospitality passes, read: "The tickets you were looking for are no longer available."

Golf.title: Is LIV Golf about to lose world ranking points?
Golf.summary: Is LIV Golf about to lose world ranking points? Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
LIV Golf waited nearly four years to secure Official World Golf Ranking points. But is that arrangement now in jeopardy? When LIV Golf finally ended its near-four year wait for world ranking points in February, those presiding over the “exhaustive” process provided a detailed explanation for their conclusions.

The Official World Golf Ranking body had eventually opted to limit points to only the top-10 finishers at each LIV event, an arrangement the breakaway league regarded as “unprecedented” victimization. But in a long-winded statement laying out its reasons, the OWGR board said it recognized a “number of areas where LIV Golf does not meet the eligibility standards set out”.

Golf.body:
LIV Golf says it has a new investor — one that CEO Scott O’Neil insists could support the league for many years to come. But behind the scenes, that confidence conflicts with player contracts that are no longer viable and a possible bankruptcy filing in the United States, both issues that must be hurdled before the new financial arrangement can be finalized.

Golf.summary: Rudy Sautron grew up on an island off the coast of Madagascar with 3 golf courses. At the U.S. Amateur, his 'dreams' have become 'goals." The post He’s from an island with 3 golf courses. He’s 3 days from a Masters invite appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Please, please ask Rudy Sautron about his wifi. Not that there’s anything wrong about his golf, which is as glorious and daring and utterly thrilling as any golfer in the field at this 126th U.S. Amateur Championship, and which pushed him into the round of 32 after many hours of toil Wednesday afternoon at Merion Golf Club. It’s just that he has been asked about his internet connection one too many times, and he is ready to set the record straight.

“People seriously ask me if I grew up with wifi,” he says, a half-smile betraying a shade of truly righteous indignation. “Do they think I grew up sleeping in a tree? Of course I had wifi! They ask me how I came to the United States. I don’t know, on a plane?!”

Golf.title: This curious Miles Russell decision in U.S. Amateur loss was tactical
Golf.summary: Miles Russell's 13th-hole birdie try in the U.S. Amateur's first round hit his opponent's mark. Here's why Russell didn't want it moved. The post This curious Miles Russell decision in U.S. Amateur loss was tactical appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Match play is all about swing moments: a smashed drive on a short par-4 that bounds up onto the green. A stuffed approach. A putt that lips in, or out. Ryder Cowan, the world’s 8th-ranked amateur and with a name made for head-to-head golf, experienced one of these moments — a decisive one — in his heavyweight, first-round bout with 4th-ranked Miles Russell at this 126th U.S. Amateur. As Cowan sized up his short-sided chip in juicy rough on the left side of the par-3 17th green, he had a 1-up lead on Russell — but also a horrid lie. Cowan chopped at it, advancing his ball all of about two inches.

Advantage, Russell, who after his own chip, from the back of the green, had about 10 feet left for his par. Cowan stared down at his ball and tried again. Out the ball popped, onto the green and . . . into the hole. Yep, another moment. Suddenly, Russell needed to hole his par try merely to extend the match. He didn’t. Cowan def. Russell, 2 and 1.

Golf.title: DP World Tour reportedly ready to fine and suspend LIV Golf members again in 2027, likely forcing decision ahead of Ryder Cup
Golf.summary: DP World Tour reportedly ready to fine and suspend LIV Golf members again in 2027, likely forcing decision ahead of Ryder Cup Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour is again taking a stand against LIV Golf. The European circuit has started notifying LIV Golf members that it will resume imposing heavy fines and suspensions as part of its conflicting events rule in 2027, according to The Athletic's Gabby Herzig. That will, in theory, force a select group of golfers to choose between the two leagues at a time in which the future of LIV Golf is incredibly uncertain.

There were eight LIV Golf members who were granted conditional releases to participate in DP World Tour events without fines or suspensions in February. Previously, at the height of the LIV Golf feud throughout the sport, golfers were hit with massive fines or suspensions for playing in unauthorized tournaments on the Saudi Arabian-backed venture. But the players — Tyrrell Hatton, Laurie Canter, Thomas Detry, Tom McKibbin, Adrian Meronk, Victor Perez, David Puig and Elvis Smylie — reached a deal to pay all previously incurred fines and play in extra DP World Tour events. That allowed them to compete on both the DP World Tour and LIV Golf in 2026.

Golf.title: U.S. Amateur’s 16-man playoff was fun for some fans, agonizing for others
Golf.summary: Sixteen U.S. Amateur contestants battled it out for 11 match-play spots at Merion on Wednesday. For some supporters, it was hard to watch. The post U.S. Amateur’s 16-man playoff was fun for some fans, agonizing for others appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — It was not yet 11 on a still, warm Wednesday morning at Merion Golf Club, but Mike and Sherry Sands needed a drink. Could you blame them? On Tuesday evening, their son, Parker, a 20-year-old rising junior at the University of Florida, needed some gut-it-out heroics on his final hole to maintain any hope of advancing to match play here at the 126th U.S. Amateur. Parker was among the wave of players who went off hole 11 at Merion, meaning his round concluded on the drivable par-4 10th.

“He had to birdie it,” Sherry began, eager to dish the blow-by-blow details only a mother can provide. “He went for it, hit the green, bounced back into the sand, and it was right on the edge, on the down slope of the trap. Like, he barely had a backswing. He had one leg out, kneeling, and he kind of, like, goes like this.” Here, Sherry contorted into an uncomfortable-looking position. “Inch from the hole,” she continued. “Wow, wow. Best shot I’ve ever seen. His caddie — he was like, ‘Best shot I’ve ever seen.”

Golf.title: This part of the bag is key for the U.S. Amateur at Merion
Golf.summary: As the best amateurs in the world begin match play at Merion Golf Club, see what part of their bag could be key at the U.S. Amateur. The post This part of the bag is key for the U.S. Amateur at Merion appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Merion Golf Club’s East course is certainly a lot more than just a the scorecard. At just 6,939 yards this week, Merion is one of the shortest courses in modern championship golf, but if you look a little closer at how the course arrives at that length, it paints a different picture.

Despite the yardage, there’s no shortage of long holes, as there are three par-4s over 480 yards (5,6 and 18), two par-3s over 230 yards — with a third that was stretched to 266 during the 2013 U.S. Open — and both par-5s measuring nearly 600 yards. On the flip side, five par-4s measure 365 yards or less, as well as a par-3 that’s just 119 yards.

Golf.title: At Merion, host of the 2026 U.S. Amateur, there's always magic in the air
Golf.summary: So many legends have won at Merion, like Hogan, Jones and Trevino. This championship, this course, follows golfers around forever. The post At Merion, host of the 2026 U.S. Amateur, there’s always magic in the air appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Mark Fulcher, the winning caddie at the 2013 U.S. Open at Merion with Justin Rose, is enduring a serious case of caddie envy this week, with the U.S. Amateur unfolding at Merion. Like all proper golf bums, Fooch (as the veteran British caddie is known throughout golf and at your better racetracks) knows that match-play golf is the game at its primal and purest best. This is, after all, a man who has caddied in seven Ryder Cups, seven Solheim Cups and one Presidents Cup, all contested at match play. The U.S. Am, like its British counterpart, is a match play event (after the two-day stroke play qualifier). At the 1930 U.S. Am at Merion, Bobby Jones completed golf’s version of the Grand Slam (it’s a bridge term) with an 8-and-7 victory in the 36-hole final over a gent named Eugene V. Homans. If you’re new to this whole thing, in match play every hole is its own one-hole contest. Jones had an eight-hole lead with seven holes to go. No more golf. Jones and his caddie, a local teenager named Howard Rexford, joyfully made the hike from the 11th green back to the club’s iconic white farmhouse clubhouse. There were no carts.

“Could you hit driver or 3-wood on one?” Fooch asked the other day, repeating a question posed to him and doing some oh-so-English stalling. The first hole at Merion is — well, what’s north of iconic? The first at Merion is a delicate tea-party par-4 with a ladies-at-lunch porch located a short lefty’s shank shot away. From there the hole is a wee uphill dogleg that, in U.S. Open stroke-play golf, is iron off the tee, wedge into the green, all day long, four straight days. But match play is a different animal.

Golf.title: LIV Golf team championship in Plymouth is canceled: report
Golf.summary: LIV Golf team championship in Plymouth is canceled: report Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
The worst-kept secret in professional golf is apparently out there now: There will be no LIV Golf event in Michigan this year. LIV has told players that the team championship event, scheduled to take place in Plymouth in three weeks, has been canceled, according to a report in The Telegraph on Wednesday, Aug. 12.

This would be the second LIV tournament to be canceled in 2026, after an event in New Orleans was called off in June. A cancellation of the event should come as no surprise. On Aug. 5, LIV announced a new lead investor but did not commit to the 2026 season finishing with the team championship at The Cardinal at Saint John's in Plymouth, scheduled for Aug. 27-30. And as Free Press columnist Carlos Monarrez pointed out, there was no visible signage or indication a tournament was coming to the course in the near future.

LIV Golf Michigan’s demise has been speculated for some time. Martin Kaymer said last month that the event had a “five percent” chance of happening, no infrastructure has been built on the host venue despite a scheduled date of Aug. 27, and a LIV announcer stated the Indianapolis event would be the final stop on the schedule. But LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil would not comment on the matter last week in New Jersey, only saying “We have not made any final formal decisions and hope to in the coming weeks.”

However, according to the Telegraph’s James Corrigan, players have now been told LIV Michigan won’t be held. As of writing, no official announcement has been made, and tickets are still available and being sold on LIV’s website.

Golf.title: LIV Golf season finale canceled, according to report
Golf.summary: LIV Golf will not host a team championship later this month, calling an end to the season earlier than expected. The post LIV Golf season finale canceled, according to report appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What has long been rumored has now been reported as reality: LIV Golf’s team championship in Michigan has been canceled. The season finale, which was scheduled for the end of August in Michigan, was already believed to be on the chopping block as early as July. Various reports suggested no on-site buildout at The Cardinal at Saint John’s, even as recently as this weekend. And now LIV is moving on, according to a report from The Telegraph, which said the league finally told its players it would not be held.

In recent weeks, most LIV players had little to say about the event, although Martin Kaymer told Today’s Golfer in late July that the team championship had about a 5% chance of happening. Now that reality finally arrived. Staffers were told to book travel home from next week’s event in Indianapolis rather than to Michigan, just a few hours up the road. And despite the dark clouds over its team championship, LIV itself has refused to announce it publicly. (When contacted by GOLF, the league declined to comment.) The event is scheduled to begin in two weeks.

Golf.title: Explained: Why LIV Golf may face another OWGR headache even if the league does survive
Golf.summary: Explained: Why LIV Golf may face another OWGR headache even if the league does survive Golfmagic
Golf.body:
One of the most tedious debates since the emergence of LIV Golf was whether or not the breakaway tour deserved to be recognised by the sport's global rankings body. Fronted by Greg Norman, the renegade tour applied for Official World Golf Ranking (OWGR) accreditation shortly after its launch in July 2022.

The application was made before the landmark 150th Open at St Andrews, but it took the governing body until the following October to reject LIV's bid. The OWGR cited several reasons for its decision and urged LIV to make adjustments to its format, field sizes and pathways into the league.

Golf.title: Best logo in golf? Even the U.S. Amateur field can't resist Merion's distinctive mark
Golf.summary: The Merion logo, or components of it, are everywhere at the U.S. Amateur this week. And for good reason: Golfers can't get enough of it. The post Best logo in golf? Even the U.S. Amateur field can’t resist Merion’s distinctive mark appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Jack Davis owns about 70 golf shirts bearing Merion Golf Club’s familiar wicker-basket-and-scotch-broom logo and maybe another 30 pieces of outerwear emblazoned with the emblem. His Merion hat tally? Anyone’s guess.

“Even for us, we’re not desensitized to it,” Davis said Tuesday afternoon here in the pro shop at Merion, which this week is the host site of the 126th U.S. Amateur. Us is the staff that runs Merion’s charming, chock-full-o-merch golf shop (Davis is the director of golf), and it is the intoxicating lure of one of the game’s most iconic logos. They’re a funny old thing, golf-club logos — most are uninspired and forgettable, some are serviceable and then there are the precious few that break through the clutter: distinctive marks that are immediately recognizable, to golfers and sometimes even non-golfers. Sleepy Hollow (headless horseman). Maidstone (spouting whale). Augusta National (no description needed). Beauties all of ’em.

Golf.title: One of the U.S. Amateur's hottest golfers has its wackiest swing
Golf.summary: Jay Leng's unique, unorthodox swing is a homemade piece of art that won him the Western Amateur and has him dreaming big this week at Merion. The post One of the U.S. Amateur’s hottest golfers has its wackiest swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Ask Jay Leng Jr. to describe his swing, and he flashes a big smile. “I’d say it’s art,” the rising junior at Stanford told GOLF after the second round of the 2026 U.S. Amateur at Merion East outside of Philadelphia.

In a previous golf era, Leng’s unique swing wouldn’t have drawn a reaction. But in the age of super-optimized, ball-speed-chasing swings, Leng’s patented motion sticks out. He and his Stanford coach, Conrad Ray, would call it “abbreviated.” Leng takes the club back inside, but before it gets to shoulder level, he turns with the club face slightly closed to start his downswing. During his follow-through, his shaft gets almost parallel to the ground and then whips the club around, finishing it however feels best for that swing. No two are the same, and he has been known to leave the ground when going after one.

Golf.title: The hidden art of preparing for a U.S. Amateur at Merion
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joey Wuertemberger has four players in the field at the U.S. Amateur. Here's how they prepared. The post The hidden art of preparing for a U.S. Amateur at Merion appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — Walking into a U.S. Amateur with four players gives you a unique perspective on preparation. They’re playing the same golf course, facing the same conditions and competing for the same championship, but that doesn’t mean they should prepare — or play the golf course — the same way. That has been one of my biggest focuses this week at Merion and Philadelphia Country Club.

My four players have very different games. One has tremendous power. Another wins with patience, positioning and putting. One relies heavily on precision and his scoring clubs, while another is a complete player who simply loves to compete. My job isn’t to give all four of them the same game plan. It’s to help each player understand where his strengths can give him an advantage, where his weaknesses can’t get exposed and how his particular game fits Merion.

Golf.title: LIV Golf just got new life but uncertainty remains
Golf.summary: LIV Golf just got new life but uncertainty remains The Week
Golf.body:
With Saudi Arabia ending its funding of LIV Golf after this season, the league is at a crossroads, moving away from its largest controversy while still in need of new financial backing. Now it appears LIV may have found some, announcing last week that it has secured investors to bring it into the 2027 season and beyond. But some major questions about the tour’s future linger.

LIV Golf has an “agreement in place with a lead investor, signed by the investor and approved by the board, to anchor the transaction and play a key role in supporting the path forward for the league’s next era, driven by and for the players,” the tour’s CEO, Scott O’Neil, said in a statement. O’Neil “didn’t identify the investor or how much money will be injected into the league,” said ESPN, though he hopes to “finalize terms in the coming weeks.”

Golf.title: The U.S Amateur's most important lesson comes from ... an accounting professor?
Golf.summary: When Brett Patterson qualified for the U.S. Open at 19, he thought golf was his future. Now he's back in the fray with a different lesson in hand. The post The U.S Amateur’s most important lesson comes from … an accounting professor? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
ARDMORE, Pa. — The U.S. Amateur Championship is a proving ground filled with lessons for golf’s youngest stars. But at this year’s edition at Merion East, one important lesson will come not from the Hugh Wilson design on the outskirts of Philadelphia, but from a 34-year-old accounting professor competing for the title.

One whose journey to the U.S. Am is different than most. Fifteen years ago, Brett Patterson was an ascending collegiate talent as a freshman at Middle Tennessee State University. At 19 years old, Patterson fired a second-round 62 at Hawks Ridge Golf Club in final U.S. Open qualifying to punch his ticket to the 2011 U.S. Open. Rory McIlroy romped to his first major title that week while Patterson shot 77-78 to miss the cut at Congressional.

Golf.title: Inside LIV Golf's wild week: Bryson, Trump and the mystery investor surfaces
Golf.summary: A frenetic week for LIV Golf at Trump Bedminster ended with appearances by President Trump and a representative from LIV's reported investor. The post Inside LIV Golf’s wild week: Bryson, Trump and the mystery investor surfaces appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BEDMINSTER, N.J. — As LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil walked the final few holes with the last group on a sweltering Sunday at Trump Bedminster, he had an inside-the-ropes special guest at his side: Ted Goldthorpe, the head of BC Partners Credit, which manages more than $10 billion globally across more than 300 investments. One of the latest companies Goldthorpe’s team reportedly has been kicking the tires on: yep, LIV Golf, which on Wednesday announced it had come to terms with an unnamed investor that will “carry and fund” the beleaguered league into 2027 and beyond.

LIV has not officially acknowledged BC Partners as its would-be funder, or lender. That news came to light via Bloomberg and the Financial Times, the latter of which reported that the deal will be consummated only if BC Partners and other possible investors receive assurances that enough of LIV’s A-listers will hang around beyond this season. Adding intrigue to the dealmaking is the fact that BC Partners is a lender to GSE Worldwide, the sports and entertainment marketing agency that represents LIV’s biggest star, Bryson DeChambeau, along with Joaquin Niemann, the 27-year-old Chilean who won his ninth LIV title here Sunday, with a three-shot win over Harold Varner. GSE said in a statement earlier this week that it had no involvement with BC Partners’ “potential financing transaction involving LIV Golf,” nor, the agency said, was it aware of any discussions happening between the two parties.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's clubs: What's the deal with his mysterious Titleist proto 3-wood?
Golf.summary: Michael Brennan won the 2026 Wyndham Championship on Sunday for his second PGA Tour win. Here's a breakdown of what's in his winning golf bag. The post Michael Brennan’s clubs: What’s the deal with his mysterious Titleist proto 3-wood? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Michael Brennan is once again a winner on the PGA Tour, earning his second PGA Tour victory and punching his ticket to the FedEx Cup playoffs at the Wyndham Championship. Brennan collected his second victory in the last three weeks for Titleist’s mysterious GTS prototype 3-wood. The 24-year-old was actually the first player to be spotted with the unknown GTS fairway wood option at the Texas Children’s Houston Open during the GTS driver launch, but didn’t game the prototype until two months later at the Charles Schwab Challenge.

Titleist has thus far not commented on the prototype, but we can speculate that the GTS may have similar characteristics to the GT1 3Tour fairway wood that both Brennan and Cameron Young — who switched to the prototype this week — previously played.

Golf.title: Michael Block walks off course at senior event, is DQ'd
Golf.summary: Michael Block received one of the strangest DQs of the 2026 golf season on Sunday, and neither side seems entirely sure why. The post Michael Block walks off course at senior event, is DQ’d appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It’s the senior tour DQ heard ’round the world, if such a thing exists. Michael Block’s disqualification from the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship in Aberdeen, Scotland was not just shocking because it was, well, a story of a DQ from a Legends Tour event. It was shocking because it arrived with a torrent of criticism, a two-shot penalty for showing up late to the tee box, a series of competing accusations … and a much, much larger dose of confusion.

So, what exactly happened? Let’s recount the facts. Things were not going well for Michael Block, senior golf sensation, at the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship. He’d posted three consecutive over-par scores at Trump International — 76-73-78 — leading into Sunday’s final round, an 11-over score that would have been good for 49th place in the competition.

Golf.title: Why men should pay attention to Asterisk Talley's winning U.S. Women's Am clubs
Golf.summary: Asterisk Talley won the 2026 U.S. Women's Amateur. How she builds the bag can teach the weekend warrior a few lessons. The post Why men should pay attention to Asterisk Talley’s winning U.S. Women’s Am clubs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Seventeen-year-old Asterisk Talley took home the trophy at this year’s U.S. Women’s Amateur at The Honors course. After multiple delays due to storms, the final match came down to Talley and No.1 seed 17-year-old Anna Iwanaga. Talley ended up victorious, winning 8&6 over Iwanaga in the 36-hole final match with nine birdies and an eagle. If you listen to our Fully Equipped Podcast, you’ll often hear us say that the women’s game has more relatable equipment to the average golfer, so let’s see what we can learn from Talley’s winning TaylorMade setup.

The good news for the guys? This is probably one of the more “crafty” women’s setups I’ve seen. It’s a fun bag. Yup. Jumbo. On all her clubs. I had a chance to hang out with Asterisk for a little bit on the range at Whirlwind Golf Club earlier this year, and it was the first thing I noticed too. I asked her about it, and she had a pretty simple answer for me.

Golf.title: Asterisk Talley's U.S. Women's Amateur win delivered the message she'd been sending
Golf.summary: Asterisk Talley's dominant U.S. Women's Amateur win was years in the making. Afterward, the message she'd been sending was finally received. The post Asterisk Talley’s U.S. Women’s Amateur win delivered the message she’d been sending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Four months ago, Asterisk Talley stood on the 12th tee at Augusta National with seven holes between her and the Augusta National Women’s Amateur title. The 17-year-old had just made her first bogey of the week at the 11th but was still in command of the tournament.

Twenty minutes later, Asterisk Talley had lost the tournament after a quadruple bogey that saw her put two balls in the water from the back bunker. After limping home with tears in her eyes, Asterisk Talley stood at the mic and showed grace as she answered questions about a brutal life lesson delivered in public. A month later at the Chevron Championship, Asterisk Talley explained that while those scars were painful, she realized they were the price of wanting to be great. That you can’t win unless you’re willing to risk being broken.

Golf.title: Michael Brennan's Wyndham win ended with touching reminder from his mom
Golf.summary: Michael Brennan won the Wyndham to make the playoffs. After his win, his mom reminded him of something else that came with his win. The post Michael Brennan’s Wyndham win ended with touching reminder from his mom appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Michael Brennan didn’t want to be done playing golf. The 24-year-old had been in contention the past two Sundays and entered the Wyndham Championship feeling like his game was finally where it needed to be. There was only one problem. After struggling for most of the year, Brennan entered the PGA Tour’s regular-season finale ranked 105th in the FedEx Cup Playoff standings. He needed a three-way tie for second or better at Sedgefield Country Club to keep his season going to Memphis.

Brennan opened with rounds of 66 and 65 to enter the weekend three shots off the pace set by Beau Hossler. A sizzling Saturday 63 pulled Brennan even with Hossler and then he put his foot on the gas on Sunday, reeling off five straight birdies on the front nine to take the lead and put the pressure on Hossler, who needed a win to keep his season alive, to catch him down the stretch.

Golf.title: Back in stock! Shop Mizuno's Pro M-13 irons
Golf.summary: Mizuno's new Pro Modern Series irons were an immediate hit when first released, and now the popular Pro M-13s are back in stock. The post Back in stock! Shop Mizuno’s Pro M-13 irons appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Mizuno’s new Pro Modern Series irons were an immediate hit when they were first released in January, and now the popular Pro M-13s are back in stock at Fairway Jockey. Featuring easy-launch technology in the long irons, more stability in the mid-irons and forged-steel construction in the short irons, the Mizuno Pro M-13s have a Tour-style look, and are designed for players looking for speed, forgiveness and playability without sacrificing Mizuno’s traditional shaping and feel.

Could the Pro M-13s be a fit for your game? “M-13 is for the player who doesn’t quite have the precision or consistency to wield a single-piece forging like the Pro S-3, or perhaps a great ball striker who would like to regain some lost speed,” wrote GOLF associate gear editor Jack Hirsh at the time of the clubs’ release. “The irons will have a wide range of handicap users and could make it into the bags of elite players as a long iron replacement.

Golf.title: Brooks Koepka offers unflinching assessment of PGA Tour season: 'Pathetic'
Golf.summary: After missing out on his final chance to make next week's FedEx Cup playoffs, Brooks Koepka offered a searing assessment of his season. The post Brooks Koepka offers unflinching assessment of PGA Tour season: ‘Pathetic’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Heading into the final regular-season event of the PGA Tour season, Brooks Koepka needed to conjure some magic. The five-time major winner left LIV and rejoined the PGA Tour in January, and the expectation was that the 36-year-old would pick up right where he left off, given the eight wins he had accumulated between 2015 and 2021. (Koepka won his 9th PGA Tour event and fifth major, the 2023 PGA Championship, while playing as a member of LIV Golf.)

But Koepka’s Tour re-entry didn’t produce the level of performance he was hoping for — at least relatively speaking. He made 10 of 15 cuts with six top-25 finishes, but never really contended for a title.

Golf.title: Niemann, Varner III and Westwood share LIV Golf New York going into last day
Golf.summary: Niemann, Varner III and Westwood share LIV Golf New York going into last day Arab News PK
Golf.body:
BEDMINSTER: Joaquin Niemann’s dominant week hit its first speed bump, but he remains well positioned to secure his second LIV Golf title of the season. The LIV Golf New York 2026 36-hole leader opened Saturday with a double bogey on the par-4 first, the first blemish on his card all week, but he battled back throughout the day en route to a 1-under 70. He heads into the final round at 14-under, maintaining the outright lead at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster.

Niemann admitted the start stung but said he was able to reset quickly. “Obviously not the best tee shot coming out to start the round, but it was kind of good to just be back into that moment,” Niemann said. “It was a little bit frustrating. I think I was able to handle it pretty good.”

Golf.body:
Unless, of course, a small child brought into question whether you could, in fact, play it as it lies. That was the bizarre question facing Wyndham Championship 54-hole leader Beau Hossler on Saturday afternoon, shortly after the horn blew in the 18th fairway forcing a stoppage in play for a band of inbound storms.

As Hossler went through the typical pro golfer’s checklist after the horn blew — mark the ball with a white flag in its position, retrieve it, put your things away, go into the clubhouse — he was greeted with an unexpected visitor. A young girl, no older than two, had stepped over the ropeline and into the field of play, prancing through the grass in the direction of Hossler.

To set the scene, the events happened during a member-member championship at WingHaven last weekend. The golfer in question, who we won’t name to avoid piling on, is a plus-2 handicap and played college golf at a junior college before having what he described to ESPN as “a cup of coffee” at Eastern Illinois University.

Bryson DeChambeau is “100 percent” confident in LIV Golf’s future after CEO Scott O’Neil announced earlier this week that the league had found a “lead investor” to keep it alive past 2026. Golf.title: Want to hit a proper pitch? Master this 1 key
Golf.summary: Top 100 Teacher Krista Dunton explains why getting too steep can cause pitching problems — and how to avoid it. The post Want to hit a proper pitch? Master this 1 key appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One key to hitting a great pitch shot is balancing steep angles in the setup with shallow angles during the motion. If you get too steep in the swing, the leading edge can dig and create inconsistent contact. Here’s how to keep that from happening.

At address, keep your hands neutral with minimal shaft lean, while your head and chest are slightly ahead of the ball. With this setup, you’ll create the necessary steepness in the body to hit a proper pitch. Now, for the shallow motion. Set the clubface open at address and un-cock your wrists.

Golf.title: Can't find a hat without a logo? Blame a refrigerator salesman
Golf.summary: How do today's pros command seven figures for a hat sponsorship? It all started at the 1968 PGA Championship ... with a refrigerator salesman. The post Can’t find a hat without a logo? Blame a refrigerator salesman appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As with most things modern in golf, Arnold Palmer played a part in the evolution of golf headwear. His win at the 1954 U.S. Amateur wasn’t just the King’s first step to the throne; photographs from his quarterfinal win are among the earliest of an elite golfer wearing a ball cap.

Flip your lid a decade-plus later: Another King — Lou, senior vice president of marketing at Amana Refrigeration — is watching Julius Boros outduel Arnie to victory at the 1968 PGA Championship in Texas. History has it that at one point in the television broadcast, Boros pulled an Amana-branded promotional hat from his golf bag to protect against the blazing San Antonio sun.

Golf.title: Brad Faxon recalls his wild ride at the '85 Honda Classic — with Michael Bamberger on the bag
Golf.summary: In 1985, Brad Faxon hired Michael Bamberger to caddie for him at the Honda Classic — and the experience made a lasting impact. The post Brad Faxon recalls his wild ride at the ’85 Honda Classic — with Michael Bamberger on the bag appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In 1985, second-year pro Brad Faxon and aspiring writer Michael Bamberger were two kids trying to figure it out. Faxon was in search of his game, Bamberger in search of a gig. Here the golfer-coach-broadcaster recalls their wild ride at the ’85 Honda Classic, where one of them passed go and the other — well, Faxon tells the rest.

On a late-fall day in 1984, after my rookie season on the PGA Tour had wrapped up, a personal letter arrived at my new townhouse in Orlando. Personal letters had a lot of impact in those days, and this one landed with a particular thud. It was written on a manual type-writer and, though the tone was modest, it went on for pages. The author told me about his own play as a bogey golfer, his experience as an occasional caddie while in high school and his first postcollege job as a reporter at a weekly newspaper on Martha’s Vineyard, an island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts. Eventually, he made his pitch: Was I looking for a caddie for the 1985 golf season, and, if so, could he throw his hat in the ring?

Just as was the case on Wednesday and Thursday here at the Honors Course, wild weather conditions halted play Friday afternoon with all eight Round of 16 matches underway. Unlike the first two days, though, on Friday play never resumed.

OLTEWAH, Tenn. – For Rachel Heck, Thursday’s 1-up victory over Anna Davis at the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur was about more than advancing to the next round. This week marks Heck’s third competitive event of the year, but it wasn’t until her match against Davis, the 2022 Augusta National Women’s Amateur champion — which came down to the final hole — that she felt something she’d been missing for a long time.

“So much excitement,” Heck said after winning her match, “It was so fun to feel those emotions again, the adrenaline and the nerves. Golf.title: The hidden value of playing golf with a pro can endure for decades
Golf.summary: Pro-ams give the duffing class an inside-the-ropes illusion that we play the same game the pros play. But there's another benefit, too. The post The hidden value of playing golf with a pro can endure for decades appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Baseball has fantasy camps but golf has something far better: the pro-am. Pro-ams give the duffing class an inside-the-ropes illusion that we play the same game the pros play. Which we do, in a limited way. Pros like to moan about the hardship of playing with us. Male pros in their golfing prime, I should say — PGA Tour stars and the like. LPGA pros have always had a better attitude about their pro-am obligations. The women seem to understand, maybe on instinct alone, that ams pay bills, and the pro-am itself connects amateur fans to their assigned pros forever.

In the early 1980s, I caddied in an LPGA pro-am on Long Island with Lori Garbacz as the headliner. She was personality-plus. I followed her in the agate type of various newspapers and magazines for the rest of her long career, and laughed out loud when I read that she had instructed her caddie to order a Domino’s pizza for on-course delivery during a crawling U.S. Open round at Colonial Country Club. So on brand, based on my half-day with Lori G. As a marketing tool, you can’t beat the pro-am. It comes right out of the long, rich history of human intercourse. People needing people, etc.
Golf.copy:
Baseball has fantasy camps but golf has something far better: the pro-am. Pro-ams give the duffing class an inside-the-ropes illusion that we play the same game the pros play. Which we do, in a limited way. Pros like to moan about the hardship of playing with us. Male pros in their golfing prime, I should say — PGA Tour stars and the like. LPGA pros have always had a better attitude about their pro-am obligations. The women seem to understand, maybe on instinct alone, that ams pay bills, and the pro-am itself connects amateur fans to their assigned pros forever.

In the early 1980s, I caddied in an LPGA pro-am on Long Island with Lori Garbacz as the headliner. She was personality-plus. I followed her in the agate type of various newspapers and magazines for the rest of her long career, and laughed out loud when I read that she had instructed her caddie to order a Domino’s pizza for on-course delivery during a crawling U.S. Open round at Colonial Country Club. So on brand, based on my half-day with Lori G. As a marketing tool, you can’t beat the pro-am. It comes right out of the long, rich history of human intercourse. People needing people, etc.

Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau caught throwing tee-box tantrum after nightmare LIV Golf start Golfmagic
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau was caught throwing a tantrum on the 5th tee box after a nightmare opening to the first round of LIV Golf New York at Trump National Bedminster. The Crushers GC captain endured one of his worst starts of the season, slipping to 4-over par through his opening four holes after a disastrous run that included a double bogey at the 1st, another bogey at the 2nd and a further dropped shot on the 4th.

Clearly unhappy with his rough start, DeChambeau took a swig from a plastic bottle before walking towards the bin on the 5th tee. In a visible display of frustration, the 32-year-old American aggressively threw his bottle at the bin, only to miss completely as it bounced off the rim and onto the grass.

Golf.title: How a signed Nelly Korda glove became a treasured gift to kids half a world away
Golf.summary: An autographed Nelly Korda golf glove made its way to a junior golf program in Brazil. But it wouldn't have happened without some help. The post How a signed Nelly Korda glove became a treasured gift to kids half a world away appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Nelly Korda’s autograph is as distinctive as her swing. She signs her first name only, with a towering “N” followed by wavy letters that could almost pass for markings on a polygraph. Like most of her peers on the LPGA Tour, Korda is generous with her John Hancock. After any given round, the number of signatures she doles out is apt to exceed the score on her card.

Fans approach her with all kinds of items: flags, programs, caps, shirts. With a few pen strokes, ordinary objects become memorabilia. Some are retained as treasured keepsakes. Others turn up on eBay. Still others make their way to places their original owners could never have imagined. Each becomes part of a story.

Golf.summary: After 36 holes of stroke play at the 2026 U.S. Women's Amateur, a nine-player playoff was needed to decide the final spots. The post 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur: Marathon 9-player playoff decides final 64 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
OOLTEWAH, Tenn. – After two rounds of stroke play at the 2026 U.S. Women’s Amateur, two players sit atop the leaderboard. Anna Iwanaga, a 17-year-old from Japan, held onto her first-round lead to earn co-medalist honors, at six under, alongside 15-year-old Hailey Kim of Simi Valley, Calif.

Just one stroke behind the co-medalists was 17-year-old Asterisk Talley, whose second-round 3-under 69 secured her the No. 3 seed entering match play. The players battled more than just one another. A weather delay of nearly two and a half hours suspended second-round play on Wednesday and forced competitors to return the following day to complete their rounds.After regular play concluded, nine players were tied at five over, with just two spots remaining in the 64-player match play field: Bridget Boczar, Paula Francisco, Sarah Lydic, Claire Swathwood, Eliana Saga, Kathryn VanArragon, Nobelle Park, Addison Klonowski and Hsin Chun Liao.

Golf.title: Hull looking to get back to 'ruthless' self
Golf.summary: Golfer Charley Hull says she is looking to get back to her ruthless self after finishing joint sixth at The Open at Royal Lytham and St Annes last weekend.
Golf.body:
Golfer Charley Hull says she is looking to get back to her "ruthless" self after finishing joint sixth in The Open at Royal Lytham and St Annes last weekend. Hull started the final day in contention, five shots behind Yealimi Noh, but shot a +1 round of 72 on Sunday as Shiho Kuwaki went on to pick up the trophy following a dramatic play-off with Esther Henseleit.

During an eventful week in which she defended herself following a prank she played on her caddie, Hull showed some exceptional touches, including a wonderful opening tee shot on Friday.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026: Full schedule, India’s top players, dates and venue
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026: Full schedule, India’s top players, dates and venue WION
Badminton.body:
The BWF World Championships 2026 are set to bring the world's best badminton players to New Delhi as India prepares to host the prestigious tournament for the second time. The 30th edition of the Badminton World Championships will be held from August 17 to 23, 2026, at the Indira Gandhi Arena in New Delhi. The week-long tournament will feature five events, men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, women's doubles and mixed doubles, with the competition progressing from the opening rounds to the finals over seven days.

According to the latest draft schedule approved by the referee, the tournament will begin with staggered opening rounds on August 17 and 18. From August 19, the competition will move into the knockout stages, with the quarter-finals, semifinals and finals scheduled from August 21 onwards.

Badminton.title: 'No fear, no revenge': Ayush Shetty’s mindset ahead Of BWF World Championships blockbuster match
Badminton.summary: 'No fear, no revenge': Ayush Shetty’s mindset ahead Of BWF World Championships blockbuster match WION
Badminton.body:
Ayush Shetty is not interested in measuring himself against the legends who came before him. As he prepares to make his BWF World Championships debut on home soil, the young Indian shuttler is instead focused on carving out a legacy of his own. “I think I don't see it as a benchmark to chase. I think I would like to set my own benchmark,” Ayush said ahead of the BWF World Championships 2026 in New Delhi.

The challenge awaiting Ayush could hardly be bigger. Drawn against world no. 1 Shi Yuqi in the opening round, the Indian knows he will have little room for error. However, rather than being overwhelmed by the prospect, Ayush insists he was prepared for whoever came his way after entering the draw as an unseeded player. “I was ready to face anyone as I was unseeded. So I think I was prepared to even play the world number one,” he said, describing his immediate reaction to the draw as simply treating it as “another match”, albeit one that promises to be a “really tough battle.”

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026 Delhi: BAI vows no repeat of Indian Open chaos
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026 Delhi: BAI vows no repeat of Indian Open chaos sportstar.thehindu.com
Badminton.body:
Badminton Association of India (BAI) copped brickbats aplenty earlier this year after the Indian Open at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi was marred by monkey intrusions, bird-related disruptions, issues with ageing infrastructure, subpar spectator facilities, and the capital’s infamous pollution.

The venue, which was originally built for the 1982 Asian Games and later renovated for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, will now open its doors again to the BWF World Championships, starting Monday, and organisers will hope to make headlines for the right reasons this time, ensuring that nothing but the sport takes centre stage. The opportunity is doubly significant given India is set to host the next Commonwealth Games and the nation’s ambitious bid for the 2036 Olympics.

Badminton.title: Men’s Doubles: Top Five Pairs to Watch
Badminton.summary: Men’s Doubles: Top Five Pairs to Watch BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Traditionally, no country has enjoyed prolonged domination in men’s doubles. Six different pairs from five countries have won the men’s doubles gold in the last six editions, reflecting how open this category has been. As the 2026 edition comes up, men’s doubles is perhaps the hardest to predict, given the number of high-quality contenders.

The first quarter of this season saw Kim Won Ho/Seo Seung Jae continue their stranglehold from the 2025, but it all changed after the BWF Thomas Cup Finals in May. Since then the world No.1 pair have appeared more beatable; other pairs, notably Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, Goh Sze Fei/Nur Izzuddin and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy have risen to the fore.

The 30th edition of the Badminton World Championships will be held from August 17 to 23 at the Indira Gandhi Arena in New Delhi.

The week-long tournament will feature five events — men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, women's doubles and mixed doubles — with the competition moving from the opening rounds to the finals across seven days.

Badminton.title: BWF World C'ships: Langur mimics brought in to stop ‘monkey business’
Badminton.summary: BWF World C'ships: Langur mimics brought in to stop ‘monkey business’ Indian Sports Home
Badminton.body:
India is hosting the championship after 17 years, the Sports Authority of India and Badminton Association of India combined to give the IGI Stadium a thorough makeover. Desperate to prevent monkeys from intruding next week's badminton World Championships at New Delhi’s Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, the organisers have opted for a rather unusual measure by roping in three professional mimics to imitate the grunts and snorts of a langur to "scare the macaques away".

It's a solution that is bound to evoke a few laughs, according to PV Sindhu but the iconic shuttler also said that it shows India's effort to make the event a success. The BWF World Championships are returning to India after 17 years and the both the Badminton Association of India and the Sports Authority of India have combined to give the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium a thorough makeover to prevent the mishaps that drew international criticism during the India Open earlier this year.

Badminton.title: 'Uniquely Indian': PV Sindhu praises langur mimicry atrists depolyes to keep monkeys away at BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: 'Uniquely Indian': PV Sindhu praises langur mimicry atrists depolyes to keep monkeys away at BWF World Championships WION
Badminton.body:
India is set to host the BWF World Championships at the Indira Gandhi indoor stadium in New Delhi from August 17-23, 2026 and the organizers have deployed unique solutions to keep the monkeys away. Specialist artists have been hired to mimic langurs to keep the monkeys and other animals away from the fans in the stand. This comes after monkeys disrupted the Indian Open in January earlier this year. Star Indian shutter PV Sindhu, meanwhile, has appreciated the unique solution to ensure safe games.

“You can laugh at the solution, but you have to love the effort. So many people are working behind the scenes to make sure India is ready to welcome the world. Our solutions may be uniquely Indian, but so are our warmth, our spirit and our hospitality. Can’t wait for the badminton world to experience it all in Delhi. See you soon!,” She posted on X with a video of an artist mimicking the voice of langurs to keep the rhesus macaques away.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: Monkey whisperers to anti-pigeon gel, Delhi leaves nothing to chance
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: Monkey whisperers to anti-pigeon gel, Delhi leaves nothing to chance The Times of India
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: As rain lashed the National Capital Region on Monday afternoon, the message at the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium in the heart of the city was clear: nothing is to be left to chance now. It is an unusual sight before a major international event: organisers taking media on a guided tour to showcase preparedness. But with badminton’s global elite arriving from Aug 17 to 23, the sports ministry, Sports Authority of India (SAI) and Badminton Association of India (BAI) are determined that the tournament avoids the irritants that had dogged Jan’s India Open at the same venue — pigeon droppings on to the court, stray dogs and simian presence in the stands and stadium complex.

For India, seeking preferred-destination status for global sporting events, the success of a World Championships returning after 17 years carries considerable weight. Among those bestowed with the responsibility to keep things smooth and running is Jabbar — Delhi’s “monkey whisperer” — part of a fourman team that uses langur calls to keep the primates away.

Badminton.body:
Bengaluru: Indian shuttlers will look to make the most of the home advantage as New Delhi is set to host the BWF World Championships, starting next Monday. Prominent names like PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen benefited from their higher ranking to a favourable draw but Karnataka’s own Ayush Shetty (in pic) had no such comfort.

The unseeded World No. 23 is pitted against China’s World No. 1 Shi Yuqi on his Worlds debut. The 30-year-old Chinese shuttler is enjoying a psychological advantage over the 21-year-old Mangalorean, with three wins in their all last three outings, including a lopsided victory of 21-8, 21-10 at the Asian Championships in Ningbo, China this April.

Badminton.title: Ashmita Chaliha Wins Maiden BWF World Tour Title At Korea Masters 2026
Badminton.summary: Ashmita Chaliha Wins Maiden BWF World Tour Title At Korea Masters 2026 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Ashmita Chaliha wins the Korea Masters 2026 to claim her maiden BWF World Tour title, becoming the first Indian to win the Super 300 event. India’s rising badminton star, Ashmita Chaliah made a remarkable comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026. She defeated China’s Han Qianxi 14-21, 21-14, 21-14 in the women’s singles final on Sunday. The victory marked the 26-year-old maiden BWF World Tour title. And she became the first Indian shuttler to win the BWF Super 300 tournament.

Chaliha played her first-ever BWF World Tour final, and had to rebound from her defeat in the opening game to fourth seed Han Qianxi. It began in a confident manner from the Indian side and they led 9-5, but the five-point runs from the Chinese side changed the game, as Han took the opening 21-14. The Indian Badminton player was coming out strong in the second game. Unaffected, Chaliha took advantage of her put and took the advantage away with a 21-14 win at the halfway point and ended the game.

Badminton.title: Korea Masters: Maiden Titles for Zhu, Chaliha
Badminton.summary: Korea Masters: Maiden Titles for Zhu, Chaliha BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Zhu Xuan Chen and Ashmita Chaliha won their first HSBC BWF World Tour titles at the VICTOR Korea Masters 2026 in Asan today. Badminton.title: BWF Korea Masters 2026: Yoo Taebin Breaks Into World Top 50 After Reaching Final
Badminton.summary: BWF Korea Masters 2026: Yoo Taebin Breaks Into World Top 50 After Reaching Final Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Yoo Taebin reaches the men’s singles final at the BWF Korea Masters 2026, securing his debut in the world top 50 after a stunning semi-final win. Republic of Korea’s Yoo Taebin has secured a major career milestone at the BWF Korea Masters 2026, reaching the men’s singles final on home soil and guaranteeing his debut inside the world top 50 when the rankings are updated next week. The 22-year-old produced one of the biggest results of the tournament by defeating top seed Okimoto Yudai of Japan 21-16, 21-18 in Saturday’s semi-final.

Since the win, Yoo Taebin is one of the most noteworthy players in the Korea Masters 2026. He has now gone into his second consecutive Super 300 final as a No.1 Seeded player. The victory is Yoo's latest success as he has climbed much higher in international badminton and last week finished runner-up at the Taipei Open. His win over Okimoto, the top single seed male that entered the tournament, was all the more brilliant. With his rank of 2nd finalized, Yoo Taebin will now have a guaranteed spot in the world top 50 for the first time. This is definitely a milestone for the young south Korean and now he can take the chance to win his first Super 300.

Badminton.title: India's Contingent Aims for Success at BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: India's Contingent Aims for Success at BWF World Championships India News Network
Badminton.body:
India will be represented by a squad of 14 shuttlers at the BWF World Championships, commencing next week at New Delhi's Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. The tournament marks a significant opportunity for the Indian team to continue a medal-winning streak that dates back to 2011. Since the event's inception, India has secured 15 medals—10 bronze, four silver, and one gold. P.V. Sindhu remains India's only world champion, having won the title in 2019, and is also the most decorated player at the Championships with five medals: one gold, two silver, and two bronze, a record she shares with Zhang Ning of China.

India has reached the podium in every edition since 2011, with the men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty winning bronze in 2025. The Indian contingent, enjoying home support, will aim to uphold this impressive tradition. The squad includes two entries each in men's singles, men's doubles, women's singles, and mixed doubles, alongside one women's doubles pair.

Badminton.title: ‘Quality of Top 20 is What Top 10 Used to Be’
Badminton.summary: ‘Quality of Top 20 is What Top 10 Used to Be’ bwfworldchampionships.bwfbadminton.com
Badminton.body:
Ahead of the upcoming BWF World Championships – her 11th – European champion Kirsty Gilmour talks about adapting to younger generations of opponents, working on becoming the best version of herself, and her connection with Indian fans.

You’ve seen different generations of opponents. What do you make of the younger ones? Is there a different approach or is it just various individual styles as before? Year on year it becomes more physical. Maybe when I was younger, I thought I would get to a point and then it would become easier. I would like ‘get it’ but because the game is always evolving, always changing, it’s never become easier to be honest, and I think the younger ones are so hungry to beat the more established players, whereas before maybe the older ones dominated, but the younger ones are always at your heels, always ready.

TOI has reliably learnt that India's leading men’s singles medal hope reached the 16-court, 40,000-square-foot facility on Thursday and began preparations with light sessions and warm-up matches. Competitor News.title: Official: Racing Santander secure deal for Athletic Club star
Competitor News.summary: Official: Racing Santander secure deal for Athletic Club star sports.yahoo.com
Competitor News.body:
Racing Santander have this week announced a transfer agreement with La Liga rivals Athletic Club. This comes amid confirmation of Julen Agirrezabala putting pen to paper on terms with the newly-promoted outfit.

Goalkeeper Agirrezabala for his part spent the duration of the 2025/26 campaign plying his trade out on loan away from parent club Athletic. After linking up with Valencia, the 25-year-old went on to endure something of a hit-and-miss time of things at Mestalla, amid competition from the more established Stole Dimitrievski.

Competitor News.title: Market news
Competitor News.body:
According to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, chief executive Ryan Cohen is considering proposing a partnership or joint venture that would enable eBay to leverage GameStop’s roughly 1,600 US retail locations.

Sources told Bloomberg that such a move could allow both to increase market share in high-margin categories such as trading cards and collectibles. It was understood that GameStop, as one of eBay’s largest shareholders, would seek representation on eBay’s board as part of any partnership.

Competitor News.title: Racing Santander close in on Julen Agirrezabala deal
Competitor News.summary: Racing Santander close in on Julen Agirrezabala deal Yahoo Sports
Competitor News.body:
Racing Santander have reached a verbal agreement with Athletic Club to sign goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala, according to comuniate.com. The move would see the Rentería-born keeper leave Bilbao to become Racing's new number one as the Cantabrian club prepares for its return to LaLiga EA Sports.

Agirrezabala has spent much of his Athletic career behind Unai Simón, though he has shown flashes of real quality when called upon, particularly in the Copa del Rey and Europa League. Last season he went out on loan to Valencia, where injuries disrupted his campaign and prevented him from establishing himself as an undisputed starter.

Competitor News.title: Liverpool in new shirt sponsor talks: Standard Chartered deal up in 2027
Competitor News.summary: Liverpool in new shirt sponsor talks: Standard Chartered deal up in 2027 This Is Anfield
Competitor News.body:
Liverpool officials are in talks with potential sponsors as their front-of-shirt and shirt-sleeve deals with Standard Chartered and Expedia will expire in 2027. This could be the final season with Liverpool wearing Standard Chartered on the front of their shirts, with the British multinational bank having sponsored the club since 2010.

Liverpool’s current agreement runs to the end of 2026/27 and is worth around £50 million a year, after an extension was signed in 2022. The same applies to shirt-sleeve sponsor Expedia, who took over from Western Union in 2020 and last agreed terms in 2023 at a projected value of £12 million per season.

Competitor News.title: #DONKOMI: Yan Diomande joins Real Madrid on seven year deal
Competitor News.summary: #DONKOMI: Yan Diomande joins Real Madrid on seven year deal citisportsonline.com
Competitor News.body:
Côte d’Ivoire winger Yan Diomande has completed a move to Spanish giants Real Madrid from German Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Real Madrid announced the signing on Thursday, August 6, bringing an end to lengthy negotiations that had at one stage appeared to stall.

The 19-year-old has signed a seven-year contract until 2033 in a deal reportedly worth €125 million, with a further €15 million in performance related add ons. Diomande is regarded as one of football’s brightest young talents, with Liverpool also reportedly interested in signing him during the transfer window.
